title: Reflection equations and Littlewood identities for spin Hall-Littlewood and $q$-Whittaker functions
abstract: We describe two-parametric Littlewood identities for inhomogeneous stable spin Hall-Littlewood and inhomogeneous spin $q$-Whittaker symmetric functions. These identities generalize the Littlewood identity found by Warnaar (2006) for the ordinary Hall-Littlewood polynomials. However, instead of Rogers-Szegö coefficients used by Warnaar, coefficients in our identities are given by products of Al-Salam-Chihara polynomials. Our proof relies on integrable lattice models. A key step includes three new solutions to the reflection and boundary equations for the fully fused six-vertex model. To find these solutions we use isomorphisms between tensor products of evaluation $U_q(L\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-modules, as well as covectors stable under a $q$-Onsager coideal subalgebra.

title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP III: The fan region
abstract: We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) in the fan region with general boundary rates. The stationary height fluctuations in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region are known to have limits involving Brownian excursions or meanders. We establish discrete counterparts of these limits: on intervals away from the boundaries, the joint law of the occupation variables is approximated in total variation distance by particle configurations constructed from lazy simple random walk excursions and meanders. In the high- and low-density phases of the fan region, we establish Bernoulli product approximations with errors that decay exponentially in the distance from the relevant boundary. Our methods combine refined combinatorial estimates for Motzkin paths and the matrix product ansatz in the totally asymmetric case with a Fourier-type decomposition (based on Askey--Wilson polynomials) of the change of measure for general asymmetry. In addition, in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region, we prove moderate deviation estimates for particle counts on arbitrary sets of sites. These estimates rely on a covariance identity for an auxiliary path measure, through which total nonnegativity (of order two) of the matrices yields negative correlations.

title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP II: The coexistence line
abstract: We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on the coexistence line. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation, together with the probabilistic interpretation, established in the first paper in this series, of the associated Bryc polynomial in terms of an inhomogeneous birth--death chain. Our main result gives a sharp approximation of the stationary measure. Specifically, we identify the shock location as an explicit observable of the particle configuration and obtain optimal bounds on the total variation distance between its law and the uniform measure on the lattice. Conditional on the shock location, we approximate, in total variation distance, the joint law of the occupation variables away from the shock by Bernoulli product measures with different densities to its left and right. These approximations lead to further applications, including fluctuation limits, moderate deviation bounds for the particle density, and limits for correlation functions under the stationary measure.

title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP I: The shock region
abstract: We investigate the role of asymmetry in the stationary measures of integrable probabilistic models with boundary interactions. This paper is the first in a series of three focusing on the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP). The stationary measure of open ASEP admits a two-layer Gibbs representation in which a correction term, which we call the Bryc polynomial, encodes the dependence on the asymmetry parameter. We give a probabilistic interpretation of the Bryc polynomial in terms of a birth-death-type Markov chain. As an application, we obtain sharp total variation approximations of the stationary measure by Bernoulli product measures in the high- and low-density phases of the shock region. These approximations yield further applications, including moderate deviation estimates for the stationary measure of open ASEP, as well as asymptotic results for the related model of open ASEP with light particles.

title: Stationary measures of the open KPZ equation: A short proof
abstract: In this note, we give a short probabilistic proof of the two-layer Brownian representation of the stationary measure of the open Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on a finite interval with arbitrary Neumann boundary parameters, conjectured by Barraquand and Le Doussal and recently established in full generality by Dunlap, Gu and Rosati. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation of the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) under Liggett's condition, together with our previously established probabilistic interpretation of the associated Bryc polynomials in terms of inhomogeneous birth--death Markov chains. Martingale estimates yield uniform asymptotics for these polynomials under weakly asymmetric scaling. Combined with known convergence results from open ASEP to open KPZ, these estimates recover the stationary height profile of the open KPZ equation as the first marginal of a reweighted pair of Brownian motions.

title: Infinite-Particle Determinantal Dynamics from Brownian Motion on $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$
abstract: We study the edge scaling limit of the logarithms of the squared singular values of multiplicative Brownian motion on the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$ with general initial conditions. Building on earlier work [arXiv:2605.06429], we prove that, for every initial condition in the enhanced state space, the limiting dynamics are determinantal and derive an explicit double-contour formula for their extended multitime correlation kernel. The dependence on the initial state, including information not determined by the particle coordinates, is encoded by the associated Laguerre--Pólya entire function. We further extend the construction of solutions to the corresponding infinite-dimensional system of singular stochastic differential equations to arbitrary initial configurations, including those with coinciding coordinates.

title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
abstract: We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition. The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures. For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $β$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $β> 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $β= 2$.

title: Stationary Measures and Boundary Correlations for Multispecies Half-Line ASEP
abstract: We construct stationary measures of the multispecies ASEP on the positive half-line, with injection of highest-priority particles at the left boundary, using vertex models. Our results extend existing constructions of Martin and Aggarwal-Nicoletti-Petrov for the full-line ASEP to the half-line. For the two-species process, we compute the joint distribution of occupation colors at the first two sites. We also partially address the connection with the half-space ASEP speed process.

title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
abstract: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/β$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $β=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $β$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.

title: The Laplace transform of the stationary measure of the open KPZ equation in the shock region
abstract: The stationary increment measure of the open Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation on a bounded interval can be represented as the independent sum of a Brownian motion and another process defined via an explicit Radon-Nikodym derivative with respect to the measure induced by a Brownian motion. In the fan region, its finite-dimensional Laplace transform was previously expressed in terms of the continuous dual Hahn process. The main contribution here consists of computing the finite-dimensional Laplace transform for a range of parameters in the shock region by an analytic continuation argument. As an application, we provide a direct proof of the convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the increment height function of open WASEP under the stationary measure in the shock region, by computing the convergence of finite-dimensional Laplace transform without relating to the open KPZ equation.

title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
abstract: This work constructs a non-trivial solution to the ill-defined two-dimensional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation at criticality: a distribution-valued stochastic process on the plane, which we call the Critical 2D KPZ Process. It arises as the limit in law of centred log partition functions of two-dimensional Gaussian directed polymers at criticality, viewed as discretised KPZ solutions. It is also a measurable function of the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) via a renormalised Cole-Hopf transformation, obtained as the limit of the centred logarithm of the spatially mollified SHF as the smoothing is removed. The Critical 2D KPZ process is non-Gaussian and its covariance displays a log-log blow-up near the diagonal. Gaussian fluctuations emerge when averaging on shrinking spatial scales. The results presented here were obtained through extensive interactions with generative AI (ChatGPT 5.5, 5.6 and 6); see Appendix C for more details. The proof builds on key recent and older advances in our field, combined in novel ways with substantial AI input. We view this manuscript as a "community project" that represents more than a decade's collective effort. We have worked on making the presentation as accessible as possible, highlighting the main ideas and their relations to the literature.

title: Painlevé representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
abstract: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $σ$-Painlevé III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $σ$-Painlevé V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.

title: First pair coalescence among three geodesics
abstract: In directed last-passage percolation with i.i.d. exponential vertex weights, the coalescence time $\operatorname{Coal}(a,b)$ of two semi-infinite geodesics started from vertices $a$ and $b$ in a fixed direction has a heavy tail with (KPZ) exponent $2/3$, and hence infinite expectation. For directed FPP and LPP with arbitrary weights, we prove that $$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\min\{\operatorname{Coal}(a,a-e_1),\operatorname{Coal}(a,a-e_2)\}\bigr]<\infty.$$ We also consider FPP and LPP models in which antidiagonal motion is allowed, and prove that for every integer $k>0$, \[\mathbb{E}\bigl[\min\{\operatorname{Coal}(a,a-k(e_1-e_2)),\operatorname{Coal}(a,a+k(e_1-e_2))\}\bigr]<\infty.\] These results support the heuristic prediction that adjacent coalescence times are negatively associated.

title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
abstract: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $θ=β/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $Nθ\toγ>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/θ$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $γ$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $β$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $γ\to\infty$.

title: The Dynamical Bead Model

We provide compelling evidence that at large space-time scales the interface exhibits diffusive behaviour, as we compute exactly its diffusivity matrix and show it is non-degenerate and independent of time.

title: Exact Microscopic One-Body Reduction in the Symmetric Exclusion Process
abstract: The symmetric exclusion process (SEP) is a paradigmatic model of interacting particle transport. Its current--density correlations are governed by an infinite many-body hierarchy of equations. Only recently, this hierarchy was found to collapse at large scales onto a single closed equation. Is this remarkable simplification created by coarse graining, or does it reflect a deeper property already present in the microscopic dynamics? Here we show that the second scenario is realized. At arbitrary time on the lattice, the entire hierarchy collapses onto a single linear equation which is exactly equivalent to a persistence problem for a single auxiliary random walker. Thus an interacting many-body problem reduces exactly to a genuine one-body problem before any scaling limit is taken. This reduction determines the complete finite-time correlation profile, including during nonequilibrium relaxation. More broadly, the microscopic operator uncovered here opens a route to more general correlation functions in the SEP, and may point to a general organizing principle for nonequilibrium interacting particle systems.

The coefficients of the correction terms are given by finite sums of Airy function or the Bessel functions of the first kind and their derivatives with polynomial coefficients. By lifting the kernel expansion to the associated Fredholm determinant, we further obtain full expansions for the largest eigenvalue distribu- tion of the Gaussian-type unitary ensembles and the smallest eigenvalue distribution of the Laguerre-type unitary ensembles. In addition, the first correction term therein involves the derivatives of the leading term.

title: The starting point of a directed geodesic is special
abstract: For any $t\in [0,1/2)$, consider the process $η_t:[0,1/2]\mapsto\mathbb{R}$ defined by $η_t(s)=Π(t+s)-Π(t)$, where $Π$ is the directed geodesic from $(0,0)$ to $(0,1)$ in the directed landscape. Let $0\leq t<u<1/2$. We show that the laws of $η_t$ and $η_u$ are mutually absolutely continuous if and only if $t>0$. This proves Conjecture 14.5 in Dauvergne, Ortmann, and Virág, 2022 in the affirmative.

title: Exact anomalous current fluctuations in the strong-anisotropy limit of the XXZ chain
abstract: We study spin-current fluctuations of the folded XXZ chain, which describes the strong-anisotropy limit of the XXZ chain. A long-time asymptotic analysis establishes that the rescaled time-integrated current converges to a non-Gaussian distribution described by the M-Wright function. The derivation relies on a nonlocal map to the one-dimensional t-0 model and its exact spin-charge separation. By extending this approach, we also show that the dynamical correlation function of the spins summed over two adjacent sites exhibits a diffusive Gaussian profile at long times.

title: Log-concavity of longest increasing subsequence
abstract: We prove a conjecture proposed by Chen that, for every fixed $n$, the sequence $(a_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave, where $a_{n,k}$ counts permutations of $[n]$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$.

title: Large spin large deviations for interacting particle systems
abstract: We propose a novel framework for analyzing the sample-path large deviations of interacting particle systems directly on a lattice by considering a large-spin limit ($s \to \infty$). Through an appropriate scaling of variables, the process concentrates around its deterministic trajectory, governed by the lattice diffusion equation. We quantify the exponential cost of observing atypical trajectories by explicitly computing the path-space large deviation rate function from the scaled microscopic generator, based on a theory due to Feng and Kurtz. The rate function is described in terms of a Hamiltonian on a lattice in terms of classical spin variables. Notably, for our main model, the symmetric harmonic process, the corresponding Hamiltonian is identified with the classical integrable non-compact Ishimori spin chain. Furthermore, we show that our large spin large deviation theory is fully consistent with traditional Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT), smoothly recovering the standard MFT Hamiltonian in the spatial continuous limit. We also perform a Poisson-noise Martin--Siggia--Rose (MSR) computation to derive the non-linear lattice Hamiltonian directly from microscopic dynamics, use a relative entropy argument to obtain the density-current action, and establish the lattice fluctuation theorem alongside its symmetry origin. Overall, our framework provides a naturally regularized, lattice analogue of MFT that circumvents spatial ultraviolet singularities and possible continuous density blow-ups. We also apply our new scheme to partial symmetric exclusion process, symmetric inclusion processes, Brownian energy process and integrable heat conduction model, showing how their large-deviation Hamiltonians relate to classical compact and non-compact spin chains.

title: Two-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equations with critical long-range correlations
abstract: We study a $(2+1)$-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equation in which the noise is correlated like $f(\log |z|)/|z|^2$ as $|z|\to \infty$. Under an appropriate rescaling and logarithmic attenuation, we show that the limiting two-point statistics are given by the solution to a forward-backward stochastic differential equation. As shown in the work of Cosco, Cottini, and Donadini (2025), with whose results our study agrees in the linear case, the interesting feature of the two-dimensional, long-range problem is that one sees a varying influence on the limiting distribution from a range of spatial scales. We show that this phenomenon appears in the decoupling function for the limiting object and that the function $f$ modulates the weight of the contribution of each spatial scale.

title: Superdiffusive Invariance Principle for the two-dimensional Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
abstract: We consider the Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process (ASEP) at its critical dimension $d=2$, started from the Bernoulli product measure with density $ρ\in (0,1)$. We first derive the sharp $\log(t)^{2/3}$ divergence of the bulk diffusivity, predicted via mode-coupling theory in [H. van Beijeren, R. Kutner, H. Spohn, Phys. Rev. Lett., 1985], including the exact prefactor, thereby removing the subleading diverging multiplicative corrections in the Tauberian bounds of [H.-T. Yau, Ann. of Math., 2004]. More importantly, we establish an invariance principle for the density fluctuation field on the corresponding superdiffusive scales. On the time scale $τ$, we rescale space by $\sqrtτ \log(τ)^{1/3}$ in the direction of the drift and by $\sqrtτ$ in the transverse direction, and prove functional convergence of the rescaled fluctuation process to the solution of a conservative stochastic heat equation with additive noise. This is the same explicit Gaussian Fixed Point obtained in [G. Cannizzaro, Q. Moulard, F. Toninelli, arXiv:2501.00344, 2025] for the two-dimensional Stochastic Burgers Equation (SBE). We also deduce a superdiffusive central limit theorem for the second-class particle under the same anisotropic rescaling. The result holds for any finite-range jump kernel with nonzero drift and uniaxial asymmetry. This is the first space-time scaling limit result for a nonequilibrium interacting particle system at the critical dimension, where Gaussian fluctuations emerge despite logarithmic corrections to the scaling. The proof uses an approximate fluctuation-dissipation relation, which is obtained by combining a sharp quantitative comparison between the ASEP and SBE generators with refined estimates on the SBE Ansatz. An additional key novelty is a tightness argument that overcomes the limitations of the Itô trick on superdiffusive scales.

title: On the composition of permutons
abstract: Permutons can be thought of as "continuum limits" of permutations of diverging size, which encode information about the number of occurrences of any given finite subpattern. We construct a natural composition operation on permutons, analogous to composition of permutations, and explore its properties via a correspondence between permutons, Markov kernels, and Markov operators. We show that no extension of permutation composition to permutons can be (jointly) continuous with respect to the usual "weak" topology on permutons, but we construct a "strong" topology with respect to which composition is jointly continuous. Moreover, we characterize strong convergence of sequences of permutations of diverging size: a sequence of permutations converges strongly if and only if it converges weakly and its limit is the transpose of the graph of a measure-preserving function. The key insight behind these results is to apply functional analysis to certain operators associated to permutons; with this shift in perspective, our results have elegant and relatively "soft" proofs. As an application, we describe the permuton limit of a product of finitely many independent uniformly sampled separable permutations and give a formula for the expectation of this limit. We also show that in this case, as the number of compositions goes to infinity, the aforementioned expectation tends to the uniform permuton.

title: Bulk universality of random regular graphs
abstract: We consider the adjacency matrix of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph on $N$ vertices. For every fixed $d\geq3$ and every fixed bulk energy, we prove that the rescaled eigenvalue point process converges to the $\mathrm{Sine}_1$ process with intensity $1/π$. We also establish universality of consecutive gaps at deterministic bulk labels and of fixed-energy correlation measures. The eigenvector input consists of polynomial estimates for mixed fourth moments on a uniformly sampled star. These estimates prevent loss of variance in the qualitative joint Gaussian limits of Backhausz--Szegedy, yielding independent variance-one Gaussian waves for fixed tuples at nearby energies. Exact switching identities then give a stationary marked flow and the microscopic loop hierarchy, which identifies the point-process limit. The appendices prove the stronger correlation and gap statements using counting-moment bounds and conditional log-gas laws for tagged limits.

title: Probing fluctuating hydrodynamics through current fluctuations in hard rod gas
abstract: We study the full counting statistics of the integrated current in a one-dimensional hard-rod gas in equilibrium, employing two recently proposed fluctuating hydrodynamic frameworks: (i) Ballistic Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (BMFT) and (ii) diffusive fluctuating hydrodynamic theory based on correlated Brownian motion approximation of hard-rod quasiparticles (CBFHD). We investigate how the predictions of these two approaches compare with each other and with the underlying microscopic dynamics. We show within BMFT that the current distribution admits a large-deviation form under ballistic scaling, and we derive an explicit expression for the large-deviation function, valid for an arbitrary inhomogeneous initial state factorized in point-particle coordinates. The corresponding current cumulants are also obtained. We subsequently analyze the current statistics within the CBFHD framework, which explicitly incorporates stochastic noise and dissipative terms, and demonstrate that the current distribution likewise obeys a large-deviation principle in this approach. We find that, while BMFT predictions for the first few cumulants and the rate function are in excellent agreement with direct numerical simulations of the microscopic hard-rod dynamics, CBFHD prediction is not. We further verify the predictions of the CBFHD independently using a collection of correlated Brownian motions, which provides an approximate description of the dynamics of hard-rod quasiparticles. Our findings indicate that CBFHD does not accurately capture large-scale current fluctuations in the hard-rod gas, whereas BMFT yields predictions in quantitative agreement with the microscopic dynamics, at least in the context of full counting statistics.

title: Cutoff for the Adjacent Transposition Shuffle on a Cycle
abstract: In the adjacent transposition shuffle on a cycle, $n$ distinct cards are placed at the vertices of a cycle, and adjacent cards swap positions according to independent Poisson clocks of rate 1. We prove that this Markov chain exhibits total variation cutoff at time $n^2\log n/(8π^2)$, with a window of order at most $n^2\log\log n$.

title: Exclusion vs Noncolliding Dynamics in Markov Processes
abstract: Let $(ξ_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a continuous-time Markov process taking values in a countable state space $E$. We consider $k$ copies of $ξ$ started from distinct positions, and write $X = (X_t)_{t \geq 0}$ for the resulting process of configurations in $E^k$. We compare two forms of interaction between the particles: the first is conditioning the particles to never collide (noncolliding dynamics), and the second is simply switching off any jumps that would cause two particles to occupy the same position (exclusion dynamics). We show under mild conditions on the tail probabilities of the collision time that the dynamics are related by an explicit exponential martingale change of measure of one another. This generalises a recent result in the integrable probability literature relating TASEP on the ring to asymmetric walkers conditioned to never collide.

title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
abstract: We establish a quantitative local law for random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three. Away from the singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum, we obtain high-probability entrywise Green's function estimates down to spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$, uniformly in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps. As a consequence, we establish complete eigenvector delocalization: every normalized eigenvector $u$ whose eigenvalue stays a small but fixed positive distance away from the singular energies satisfies $\|u\|_\infty\leq(\log N)^C/\sqrt{N}$ with high probability.

title: Continuity of the phase transition for long-range Bernoulli percolation with exponential decay on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$

title: Path space large deviation on a lattice for interacting particle systems
abstract: We investigate the path space large deviation principle (LDP) for a class of interacting particle systems on a fixed finite discrete torus. As an illustrative example, we use the partial exclusion process with maximal occupation of $s$ particles. We first verify the standard Kurtz-type law of large numbers for the original and tilted processes, thereby identifying the deterministic flows around which the large deviations are formulated. We then establish the path space LDP, with speed $s$, and identify the associated rate function in variational form as the Legendre transform of a nonlinear Hamiltonian. The proof relies on martingale techniques, exponential tightness, and a change-of-measure argument based on exponential tilting, which renders atypical trajectories typical under a modified dynamics. We also explain how the same strategy extends to further interacting particle systems. The inclusion process illustrates the conservative non-compact finite-jump case. The harmonic process is qualitatively different: a single transition may move a variable number of particles, and the limiting Hamiltonian is logarithmic with a non-trivial domain. This places the harmonic process outside the usual finite-reaction framework for density-dependent Markov jump processes. Finally, we discuss continuous-state energy-exchange models, such as the Brownian energy process and an integrable heat-conduction model, to indicate how the same Hamiltonian large-deviation formalism appears beyond discrete-state particle systems.

title: Learning Cole-Hopf Coordinates for Stochastic Growth Dynamics: the KPZ class
abstract: Inferring effective equations from observations of nonlinear stochastic processes is challenging because individual trajectories are noisy realizations, while the relevant physical information is encoded in ensemble statistics. We introduce a data-driven framework that learns a change of variables in which nonlinear stochastic dynamics become linear. The model combines a neural change of representation with a linear stochastic latent evolution and is trained through a short-time moment-matching objective, thereby avoiding trajectory \rev{simulation} during optimization. This construction yields an interpretable generative model: both the learned transformation and the latent evolution operators can be directly inspected. We validate the method on the one-dimensional Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation, a paradigmatic model of stochastic growth for which the Cole--Hopf transformation maps the nonlinear dynamics to the stochastic heat equation. From simulated height trajectories alone, the model recovers the local exponential Cole--Hopf map and the associated linear stochastic operator. Generated trajectories reproduce the main statistical signatures of the KPZ universality class, including the growth law $\mathrm{Var}(h^{t})\sim t^{2β}$ with $β=1/3$ and the GOE Tracy--Widom height distribution for flat initial conditions. These results show that interpretable stochastic equations can be inferred from data by learning representations in which the dynamics closes in a simple form. Furthermore the development of the physical informed learning permits to get insights on the physics of the dynamical process.

title: Quantum K-structure constants and cylindric Grothendieck polynomials for Grassmannians
abstract: We use the partition functions of a five-vertex exactly solvable lattice model from statistical mechanics to give new combinatorial formulae for the Schubert structure constants of torus-equivariant quantum K-theory rings of Grassmannians. The proofs build on our earlier results where we identified the transfer matrices of these lattice models geometrically as multiplications by the Hirzebruch $λ_y$ classes of the tautological subbundle and the (dual) quotient bundle. The structure constants are solutions of a system of linear equations with coefficients given by the partition function. This system may be solved explicitly by specializing the Hirzebruch parameter $y$ to an equivariant parameter, leading to explicit formulae using Cramer's rule. Furthermore, we give an alternative combinatorial construction of the partition functions in terms of sums over cylindric set-valued tableaux, which we call cylindric Grothendieck polynomials. The latter generalise McNamara's factorial skew Grothendieck and Yeliussizov's modified Grothendieck polynomials and can be thought of as an equivariant K-theoretic version of Postnikov's toric Schur function. We also provide new polynomial representatives for equivariant K-theory classes of Richardson varieties and their variants.

title: Compression Formula for Nonattacking Fillings of Non-symmetric Macdonald Polynomials
abstract: Macdonald polynomials are an important family of orthogonal polynomials that have applications to statistical physics. Corteel, Mandelshtam, and Williams proved a combinatorial model involving multiline queues for partitions; however, their work does not apply to weak compositions in general. We conjecture a first step towards this direction via a variant of the nonattacking filling model for nonsymmetric Macdonald Polynomials $E_μ$. This new model compresses the classical nonattacking filling model of Haglund, Haiman, and Loehr and mirrors the concept of trivial pairs in the multiline queue model. We prove it for a large family of weak compositions and explain the difficulty of extending this proof to the general case.

title: Scaling Limits of Density Fluctuation Fields of the Symmetric Partial Exclusion Processes Approaching the Zero Range Process
abstract: We study equilibrium fluctuations for the symmetric partial exclusion process (SPEP) on the one-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, an interacting particle system in which each site is occupied by at most $α$ particles. We assume that the jump rate is decomposable and that the instantaneous current admits a gradient form. Our aim is to study the scaling limit of the density fluctuation field of the SPEP starting from an invariant measure and to derive the corresponding stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE). A distinctive feature of our setting is that the maximum number of particles per site depends on the scaling parameter $n$ as $α=α_n \propto n^a$ for some $a>0$, so that the model interpolates between the partial exclusion process ($α<\infty$) and the symmetric zero range process (SZRP, $α= \infty$). Under the diffusive rescaling in which the lattice spacing is $1/n$ and time is accelerated by a factor $n^2$, we prove that the density fluctuation field converges to the solution of the stochastic heat equation. The limiting SPDE coincides with the one obtained for the SZRP. A key ingredient in the proof is the convergence, under a suitable rescaling, of the partition function of the reversible measure of the SPEP to that of the SZRP. This convergence implies that expectations of a wide class of local functions under the reversible measure of the SPEP converge to the corresponding expectations under the reversible measure of the SZRP, and provides a rigorous sense in which the SPEP approximates the SZRP as $n\to\infty$.

title: Determinantal linear spanning forests
abstract: We introduce a determinantal linear process on the space of $1$-forms over a weighted graph endowed with a unitary local system, which we call the determinantal linear spanning forest (DLSF). This process is the analog of the uniform spanning tree in the presence of an arbitrary rank $n$ quenched gauge field in ${\rm U}(n)$ (or ${\rm O}(n)$, ${\rm SO}(n)$, ${\rm SU}(n)$, ${\rm Sp}(n)$), and generalizes the determinantal random cycle-rooted spanning forest which corresponds to the case of ${\rm U}(1)$ and ${\rm SU}(2)$. We describe the support of this process by means of a polymatroid which is described in terms of the circular and bicircular matroids. We also explain how the DLSF relates to the computation of currents in an electrical network in the presence of a gauge field. The partition function of the DLSF is shown to be the determinant of the twisted Laplacian, for which we also give a matrix-tree type theorem that computes its characteristic polynomial. We initiate the study of the twisted Laplacian determinant as a functional on the space of connections, and give a first order expansion of it in a neighborhood of the trivial connection, for which we provide a probabilistic interpretation. We extend the construction to infinite graphs, exhibiting the analogs of the classical wired and free distributions on spanning forests. We give a sufficient geometric condition on the local spectral gap for the existence of a Poincaré inequality as well as the uniqueness of the infinite volume measure, and the exponential decay of correlations. We show that on any recurrent graph, the wired and free DLSF coincide. We construct examples where they do not, for example, unlike in the classical case, on $\mathbb Z^d$ for $d\geq 3$.

title: Directed fractal percolation and non-Lipschitz variants
abstract: While models of undirected and directed geometry in random i.i.d. disorder with rapidly decaying tails are expected to behave similarly and exhibit features of the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang universality class, the scenario when the background noise is fractal is expected to be significantly different. A canonical example of the latter is Liouville Quantum Gravity, where the planar Gaussian free field forms the fractal background. A toy model capturing some of the essential features is given by Mandelbrot's fractal percolation, a random Cantor set. In the simplest setting, dyadic cubes of different scales are retained independently with probability $p$ (a parameter of the model), and the intersection of all retained cubes forms the set of open sites. Connectivity properties of such sets have been intensely studied. Across [CCD88, Cha95], a surprising result was proven. Namely, while there is a phase transition for connectivity of the fractal percolation set (like in usual bond percolation), directed percolation never occurs. Results of a similar spirit have been obtained in geometric measure theory as well. As a step towards understanding last passage percolation (LPP) driven by the Gaussian free field (initiated in [GGN24]), we study the problem of quantifying LPP in fractal percolation. Developing a multi-scale framework, we show an almost polynomial gap from linear growth of the passage time. The obstruction to high LPP values is the Lipschitz nature of directed paths. Along these lines, [Cha96] showed that any connected subset of fractal percolation must have Hausdorff dimension strictly larger than one. We show that one can construct directed paths passing through open sites in fractal percolation provided they move exponentially fast in the spatial direction---a model we introduce and term as unrectifiable directed percolation.

title: An elementary approach to the Szegő theorems
abstract: The strong Szegő theorem and the Fisher-Hartwig formula describe the asymptotic behavior of determinants obtained by restricting translationally invariant operators to large finite regions. In particular, Szegő's theorem states that, beyond the leading extensive contribution to such a determinant, there is a universal finite correction, $\sum_{r>0} rV_rV_{-r}$ where $V_r$ are the Fourier coefficients of the logarithm of the symbol. Although this formula appears throughout analysis and mathematical physics, the origin of its quadratic form and of the weight $r$ is often obscured in its standard analytic derivations. We develop an elementary picture in which the strong Szegő term arises from boundary leakage: paths contributing to the matrix exponential leave the finite interval and subsequently return. Counting the shortest such excursions immediately produces the factor $r$. We then show that an isolated boundary contributes exactly one half of the strong Szegő correction, while the two boundaries of a long interval decouple. For finite-range matrices this gives a rigorous and intuitive elementary derivation of the asymptotics, with extensions to sufficiently rapidly decaying interactions. A complementary free-fermion argument provides a physical interpretation of the same cancellation mechanism. Numerical examples illustrate the asymtotics in the well controlled regime, the Fisher Hartwig logarithmic correction. The boundary formulation does not itself require translation invariance and therefore suggests natural extensions to disordered systems, higher dimensions, and symbols with internal matrix structure. To illustrate this we numerically go beyond the formal applicability region of the Szegő formula, considering slow decay and disordered cases, and showing in some cases a robustness of the approach even for slowly decaying but disordered potentials.

title: Kardar-Parisi-Zhang superdiffusion in chaotic quantum circuits
abstract: We construct a family of chaotic brickwork quantum circuits exhibiting superdiffusive transport with dynamical exponent $z=3/2$ in the full Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) universality class. Using nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamics, we derive the propagation velocity, broadening scale, and universal scaling form of the charge correlation function from microscopic equilibrium properties. Tensor-network simulations of a two-site spin-$1$ (qutrit) circuit reproduce these parameter-free predictions, including the full stationary KPZ profile. We further construct a three-site spin-$\frac12$ (qubit) circuit, where transport varies from diffusive to superdiffusive with the chemical potential, while long-lived coherent quasiparticles delay the convergence of the profile to the KPZ scaling form. Our results establish that KPZ superdiffusion in quantum systems is not restricted to fine-tuned integrable models.

We further illustrate a scaling protocol that in principle enables unbounded increase in lifetimes in the thermodynamic limit. Our results showcase classical-like excitations originating from unitary quantum dynamics, away from the semi-classical regime, and in regions where interactions cannot be treated perturbatively.

title: Complete Factorial Asymptotics and Integrable Structure of Generalized Charlier Recurrence Coefficients
abstract: We study the monic recurrence coefficients of the generalized Charlier polynomials associated with the discrete weight \[ ρ_μ(k) = \frac{μ^k}{(k!)^2}, \qquad k\in\mathbb N_0, \qquad μ>0. \] We establish complete factorial asymptotics for the deviations $β_n-n$ and $μ-γ_n$, proving that they are beyond all algebraic orders and appear at the scale $μ^{n}/(n!)^2$. The key step is a parametrization $β_n-n=\sqrtμ\,c_nc_{n+1}$, $γ_n=μ(1-c_n^2)$, which reduces the problem to a positive sequence $(c_n)$ satisfying a discrete Painlevé II equation. Linearization around $c_n=0$ yields a discrete Bessel equation whose recessive solution is $J_n(2\sqrtμ)$. We prove that the ratio $c_n/J_n(2\sqrtμ)$ converges to a finite limit $L(μ)$, which we identify exactly as $L(μ)=1$ by combining Bessel comparison with a global analysis based on the sector decomposition of the associated Hankel determinant. This yields the exact connection formula \[ c_n \sim J_n(2\sqrtμ), \qquad n\to\infty, \] and consequently the precise asymptotics \[ β_n-n\sim \frac{μ^{n+1}}{n!(n+1)!}, \qquad μ-γ_n\sim \frac{μ^{n+1}}{(n!)^2}. \] We further develop a complementary approach based on Hankel determinants interpreted as a discrete logarithmic gas. We show that the Hankel determinant factorizes as $Δ_n(μ)=μ^{n(n-1)/2}T_n(μ)$ and admits a sector decomposition $T_n(μ)=1+\sum_{q=1}^{n}S_q(μ)$ with sector contributions independent of $n$. We establish $S_q(μ)\sim e^μμ^q/(q!)^2$, providing an independent derivation of the factorial corrections. Together, the Bessel comparison and sector decomposition reveal a rich integrable structure linking discrete Painlevé dynamics, Toda deformations, and Hankel--partition representations.

title: Iwahori Whittaker functions for unramified quasi-split groups

We then connect these operators to the Whittaker functions, establishing formulas for calculating all values for a basis of Iwahori Whittaker functions and giving a new proof of the Casselman-Shalika formula for the spherical Whittaker function. In doing so we build on the work for split groups of Brubaker, Bump and Licata; the new feature here is the appearance of a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters.

This family allows to make every operator in this regime spectrally equivalent to a singular Jacobi operator. Using these singular representatives, we apply the method of [BJK] to construct covers by $O(q_n)$ intervals of total length $O(q_n^{-1})$, improving to $O(q_n^{-2})$ on the isotropic boundary, where $q_n$ is the denominator of a canonical approximant to $α$. The covers give upper box bounds and, with packing estimates, examples where the box-counting dimension fails to exist.

title: Anomalous Mobility Enhancement in Restricted Geometries
abstract: We investigate the effect of geometrical confinement on driven transport in anomalous media within the framework of the quenched trap model. The particle performs a biased random walk on a lattice, where quenched disorder introduces power-law distributed trapping times. We consider channels that are infinite along one direction and have a finite cross-section in the remaining $d-1$ directions. In the glassy regime, where $α=T/T_g<1$, we derive an analytical expression for the mean longitudinal displacement in the long-time and weak-force limits. We find the scaling $\langle x_\parallel(t)\rangle \propto F_\parallel^αt^αΩ^{-(1-α)}$, where $F_\parallel>0$ is the effective longitudinal force and $Ω$ is the number of sites in a transverse cross-section. Thus, the anomalous mobility is enhanced for narrower channels. Our analytical result applies to general Bravais lattices in $d$ dimensions with periodic transverse boundary conditions. Numerical simulations confirm the analytical predictions for different lattice geometries and show quantitative agreement even for channels with reflecting boundary conditions.

title: Typicality of entanglement growth and transport fluctuations in quantum symmetric exclusion processes
abstract: We use macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to establish the typicality of charge-transfer statistics and entanglement dynamics in the quantum symmetric exclusion process, a model of stochastically hopping free fermions with diffusive transport and long-range quantum coherence. We show that the leading long-time charge-transfer full counting statistics of individual noise realizations coincide almost surely with those of the classical symmetric exclusion process (SSEP), in equilibrium and following quenches from arbitrary occupation-diagonal product states. Our results apply to transient fluctuations in the thermodynamic limit, extending previous work that has primarily focused on stationary regimes. Our approach compares the noise averages of the charge-transfer generating function and its inverse. The former reduces to SSEP, while the latter maps to an auxiliary Brownian energy process whose MFT saddle-point problem is related to that of SSEP, yielding matching large-deviation exponents. Through free-fermion identities relating entanglement to subsystem-number fluctuations, this establishes the self-averaging of the covariance-matrix eigenvalue distribution and of Rényi and von Neumann entropies. We obtain asymptotically exact predictions for entanglement growth from domain-wall and Néel initial states, in excellent agreement with numerical simulations.

title: Classification of Finite-Dimensional Simple Novikov Algebras and Their Irreducible Bimodules in Positive Characteristic
abstract: We give a complete classification of finite-dimensional simple Novikov algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, including families missing from earlier classifications in \cite{Osborn1992, Xu1996}. We determine explicit normal forms and all isomorphisms between them, and classify all nontrivial irreducible bimodules over these algebras.

title: On Gill's problem with anomalous diffusion
abstract: The classical formulation of Gill's theorem establishing the linear stability of the buoyant flow in a vertical porous channel subject to transverse diffusion and bounded by impermeable walls is here reconsidered from the perspective of anomalous mass diffusion. Anomalous diffusion is a physical effect implying a more general formulation of the governing equations of mass transfer either in a fluid or in a fluid-saturated porous medium. Anomalous diffusion is mathematically modelled via a diffusion equation with a time-dependent mass diffusivity. In this study, the stationary and parallel buoyant flow in a vertical porous layer saturated by a fluid is investigated. The implications of the anomalous diffusion model for the proof that such a flow is always linearly stable are analysed.

title: The $e$-expansion of integral form Macdonald polynomials
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the expansion of the integral form Macdonald polynomials $J_μ(x;q,t)$ in the elementary symmetric function basis. Motivated by the connection between chromatic symmetric functions and LLT polynomials, we conjecture the $e$-positivity of a normalization of $J_μ(x;q,t)$. We verify the conjecture when $μ$ is either a hook or a two-column partition. In the hook case, we express the $e$-coefficients as weighted sums over compositions. In the two-column case, we derive explicit formulas for the $e$-coefficients.

title: Combinatorial decompositions of strict partitions and multi-sum Rogers-Ramanujan type identities
abstract: While multi-sum Rogers-Ramanujan type identities have been extensively investigated through Bailey pairs, the constant term method, complex contour integration, and related techniques, many still lack an intrinsic combinatorial understanding. In this paper, we establish combinatorial interpretations for several families of triple-sum identities via structural decompositions of strict partitions. For one of these families, we extend the underlying combinatorial framework to obtain a general $(m+1)$-fold multi-sum identity. Leveraging these partition-theoretic interpretations, we construct explicit bijective proofs for all the corresponding identities. As an application, this constructive approach naturally yields some parameterized generalizations.

title: The Formal Critical Coupling of the Four-Dimensional Anderson Model
abstract: In this work we present a formal renormalization-group (RG) calculation for the weakly coupled four-dimensional elliptic Anderson model. Under a scale-independent bare-coupling convention, and with the normalization $λ_{\varepsilon}$, the bubble-chain resummation yields the geometric series $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(λ)$, with a formal pole at $λ_c$. We stress that this pole is a feature of the formal bare bubble series. The argument combines Bogoliubov-Parasiuk-Hepp-Zimmermann (BPHZ) renormalization, a Hepp-sector motivated restriction to the bubble-chain subclass for explicit resummation, and an explicit summation of the resulting geometric series. Numerically, we illustrate the analytic building blocks of the formal expansion: the massive Green function, the bubble integral, the geometric resummation, the extraction of the formal pole from synthetic noisy data, a kurtosis diagnostic, and a phase diagram of the formal variance. These computations visualize the deterministic kernels and the formal resummation used above. Using spectral methods and nonlinear least-squares fitting, we verify the short-distance asymptotic behaviour of the massive Green function for $G=(1-Δ)^{-1}δ_0$, reproduce the logarithmic divergence of the bubble integral in four dimensions, compute the formal effective variance $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(λ)$ arising from the bubble-chain resummation, locate the formal pole at $λ_c$, and draw a schematic phase diagram of the formal variance in the $(λ,\log\varepsilon)$ plane. The kurtosis diagnostic uses a synthetic proxy for the non-Gaussian regime; the sharp change is imposed by construction. Nonlinear fitting of synthetic data recovers the formal pole within the statistical uncertainty of the synthetic noise. Our results illustrate the analytic formulas and the fitting procedure.

title: Optimal Rates in Local and Central Limit Theorems for the Elephant Random Walk
abstract: We determine the optimal rates of convergence in the local and central limit theorems for the one-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes, $0\le p\le3/4$. For every fixed initial distribution, we treat both exact finite-time centering and standardization and the normalization $S_n/\sqrt n$ (or $S_n/\sqrt{n\log n}$ at criticality). We establish uniform Edgeworth expansions for local probabilities and distribution functions, and use these expansions to derive the optimal convergence rates, which exhibit several phase transitions depending on the symmetry of the initial distribution, the normalization, and the type of approximation. Our approach uses elephant polynomials for precise characteristic-function expansions and a random recursive tree representation for global Fourier bounds.

title: A functional central limit theorem for particle systems under polynomial growth conditions, with applications to statistics
abstract: We establish a functional central limit theorem (CLT) for fluctuations of time-integrated functionals of empirical measures arising from interacting McKean--Vlasov particle systems. Our framework allows for coefficients with unbounded spatial growth and dependence on arbitrarily high-order moments of the measure variable, extending the scope of the existing fluctuation theory. The proof uses a novel approach combining linear functional differentiation with new well-posedness results and estimates for perturbed backward parabolic equations in polynomially weighted Schauder spaces, yielding a martingale-type representation of the fluctuations with an asymptotically negligible remainder. The limiting process is shown to be centred Gaussian with an explicit covariance structure. As a statistical application, we derive the asymptotic theory underlying hypothesis tests for both the temporal constancy of population characteristics and parametric restrictions on the drift coefficient.

title: An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense signed random combinatorial matrices
abstract: Let $M_n$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{-1, 0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ nonzero entries, with $d=pn$ for some fixed constant $p\in(0,1/2]$. A recent result by one of the authors gives a lower bound of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of this model with high probability. In this paper, we establish a matching upper bound for $s_n(M_n)$. Specifically, there exists a constant $C_p>0$ depending only on $p$ such that \[ \forall \varepsilon >0 \qquad \mathbb{P} \left( s_n(M_n) \le \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\varepsilon^2 n} \right) \ge 1-C_p\left(\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\right). \] Consequently, in the dense regime, the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of signed random combinatorial matrices is typically of order $n^{-1/2}$.

title: On optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent reward
abstract: In this paper we consider optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent rewards. Our focus is on the following two problems: selecting one of the r best observations (Gusein-Zade's problem with full information) and minimizing the expected rank (Robbins' problem). In both settings we provide full characterization of the optimal stopping rules and corresponding optimal values. We also present numerical experiments in which the derived dynamic programming recursions are implemented, and approximations to optimal values are computed.

title: Non-equilibrium density fluctuations for the stirring process with weak boundary dynamics
abstract: We consider the one-dimensional stirring process on the segment $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, coupled to boundary dynamics that inject particles from the right reservoir and remove particles from the left reservoir, each acting on a window of size $K$. We investigate the non-equilibrium fluctuations of the system, starting from a product measure associated with a smooth initial profile. The limit Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is given in terms of the Laplacian and gradient operators acting on test functions satisfying time-dependent Robin boundary conditions that are obtained by linearizing the boundary conditions in the hydrodynamic equation. A central ingredient in our analysis is the derivation of sharp bounds on the space and space-time $v$-functions of arbitrary degree for the centered occupation variables; these bounds were proved in the companion article \cite{birmpa2025nonequilibriumfluctuationsstirringprocess}.

title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs
abstract: Let $T_n$ be the number of triangles in the Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ with $n^{-1/2}\ll p\ll1$ and fix $η\in(0,1)$. We study the large deviation rate of the lower tail event $T_n\leη\mathbb{E}[T_n]$, and the typical structure of $G(n,p)$ conditioned on this event. By earlier work [16,19,21,49], both the rate and the structure are governed by a variational problem over graphons. In this work we solve this variational problem for every $η\in(0,1)$. We show that every minimizer is either a constant graphon or a step graphon with two blocks of equal size. Correspondingly, the conditioned graph is close to an Erdős-Rényi graph or to a symmetric stochastic block model with two blocks. These two regimes are separated by a first order phase transition at the threshold $η_*=0.009217\ldots$. This resolves a conjecture of Zhao [78] and an open problem of Janson and Warnke [39] on triangles. It thereby gives a complete description of the lower tail of triangle counts in this range of $p$.

title: Block Toeplitz Operators, Matrix Valued Truncated Toeplitz operators, and Conjugations
abstract: In this paper, we characterize the complex symmetry of block Toeplitz operators on the Hardy-Hilbert space H2(E) with conjugation C_{u,λ}, where E is a finite dimensional Hilbert space. We also extend the application of this conjugation to matrix valued truncated Toeplitz operators.

title: Free energy fluctuations of symmetric perceptron models up to and including criticality
abstract: We study the free energy fluctuations of spherical and Ising perceptron models with general even activations. These include the symmetric binary perceptron, the $U$-perceptron, and the bipartite Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main result is a Gaussian CLT for the free energy that holds both in the ``high-temperature'' interior of a second moment RS regime and on its ``critical'' boundary. At criticality, the CLT has scale $(\frac{\log N}{6})^{1/2}$, which matches the free energy fluctuations of the critical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model and suggests this scaling is universal. The proof shows that the perceptron model's free energy fluctuations are explained, up to an additive $o(1)$ error with high probability, by those of a corresponding spherical Hopfield model, and that this relation persists even at criticality. This proof strategy builds on a critical reweighted moment method developed by the first and third authors \cite{du2026fluctuations} to identify the critical fluctuations of the SK free energy, which links these fluctuations to the spectral edge spacing of the disorder.

title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
abstract: For a $Δ$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{Δ/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $Δ\geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erdős-Rényi setting. In contrast, for $Δ=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to be different. Moreover, conditioned on the upper tail event of cycle counts in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, we show that the random graph contains a disjoint collection of clique and biclique like structures with probability approaching to one, a stark contrast compared to the Erdős-Rényi setting. In the complementary regime, i.e.~for $1 \ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H} \ll (\log n)^{α^*_H/(α^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges in $H$, $α^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including the regular case), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erdős-Rényi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all of the unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.

title: A paintbox characterization of labeled partitions
abstract: We study pairs of labeled random partitions $(Π,τ)$ with a finite label set $E$, which can be thought of as a random mutation and coalescence mechanism of a countable number of blocks. Labeled exchangeable partition probability functions (LEPPFs) are defined via labeled analogues of Kingman's paintbox partitions. They satisfy normalization, symmetry and consistency in a multivariate sense. Under an equivariance condition, a representation for $(Π,τ)$ in terms of labeled paintbox partitions is derived, leading to a full characterization of LEPPFs by a unique probability measure $G$. This representation is extended to jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs using a product measure $F \otimes G$. These results yield a one-to-one correspondence between distributions of jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs and pairs of exchangeable distributions and LEPPFs.

title: Central limit theorem for the Smoluchowski--Kramers approximation
abstract: We establish the central limit theorem (CLT) for Smoluchowski--Kramers approximation of Langevin equations with state-dependent, possibly non-symmetric friction and multiplicative noise. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first such result, even in the case of constant friction and additive noise. The result differs in an essential way from classical averaging CLTs and reveals a new two-scale fluctuation phenomenon. The normalized difference process retains a persistent fast component and is generally not tight in $C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)$, thus the usual continuous-path CLT cannot hold. We derive an exact decomposition of the normalized difference into an accumulated slow fluctuation and a rapidly relaxing velocity correction. The auxiliary slow fluctuation converges to a linear diffusion driven by both the original Brownian motion and an additional independent Brownian noise whose effective covariance is characterized explicitly through a quadratic Poisson corrector. For every fixed $t>0$, the fast correction converges conditionally to its local Gaussian equilibrium. Consequently, the fixed-time fluctuation limit is identified as a Gaussian mixture: $$ \frac{\bar X_t-X_t^\varepsilon}{\sqrt{\varepsilon}} \Longrightarrow \bar Y_t+N^{1/2}(\bar X_t)ξ, $$ where $\bar X_t$ is the overdamped limit, $\bar Y_t$ is the limiting slow fluctuation, $N$ is the covariance of the terminal velocity correction and solves a Lyapunov equation, and $ξ$ is a standard Gaussian random variable independent of $(\bar X_t,\bar Y_t)$. A quantitative convergence rate is also provided. The result fills the remaining gap in the asymptotic theory of the overdamped approximation at the central limit scale, complementing the existing law of large numbers, moderate deviation and large deviation results.

title: Normal form approach to unconditional well-posedness of the periodic stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation with an additive noise
abstract: We develop a stochastic normal form method for stochastic dispersive equations. As a model example, we study the stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation (SKdV) with an additive noise, posed on the circle. By replacing integration by parts (in time) in the deterministic setting with Ito's product formula in the current stochastic setting, we transform SKdV with an additive noise into a stochastic normal form equation with additive and multiplicative noises. We then use the stochastic normal form equation to prove optimal pathwise unconditional global well-posedness of SKdV in $L^2(\mathbb{T})$.

title: Large Deviations in Stochastic Dynamics: A Hamiltonian Perspective
abstract: These lecture notes present an introduction to large deviations in stochastic dynamical systems, adapted from a lecture series given at the Les Houches school ``Large Deviations: Theory and Applications'' in July 2024. The exposition develops the theory through a unified methodology: WKB analysis of backward Kolmogorov equations, which reveals the Hamiltonian structure underlying all large deviation principles considered here. We treat three asymptotic regimes systematically. First, the small-noise limit for stochastic differential equations and the large-volume limit for Markov jump processes, where the Large Deviation Principle emerges from the Law of Large Numbers through progressively finer characterizations of fluctuations. Second, the long-time limit combined with small noise, yielding the quasipotential formalism for metastability and transition rates in both equilibrium and nonequlibrium systems. Third, the long-time limit at finite noise, connecting to spectral methods via tilted generators and enabling reduction of multiscale systems. We survey computational approaches including minimum action methods, their geometric variants for quasipotential calculations, and neural network techniques. The Schlögl model of chemical bistability serves as a running example, illustrating both scalar and spatially extended settings. Appendices provide self-contained background on stochastic calculus and Markov jump processes.

title: Moduli spaces of logarithmic connections associated with difference Painlevé equations of type $E^{(1)}_n$
abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit correspondence between moduli spaces of parabolic logarithmic connections on the projective line with spectral type $(2^2,1^4,1^4)$ and $(3^2, 2^3, 1^6)$, and the spaces of initial conditions for difference Painlevé equations with symmetry of type $E^{(1)}_7$ and $E^{(1)}_8$, respectively. Furthermore, we realize the extended affine Weyl group symmetries of the space of initial conditions in terms of connections.

title: Third and Fourth Moment Phenomena for Monochromatic Edges and Applications to Graph-Based Two-Sample Tests
abstract: Given a graph sequence $\{G_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, denote by $T_n$ the number of monochromatic edges when the vertices of $G_n$ are independently colored red or blue with probabilities $p$ and $1-p$, respectively. We characterize the asymptotic normality of $T_n$, after centering and scaling to unit variance, in terms of subgraph (motif) counts and standardized moments. One of the highlights of our results is a {\it third moment phenomenon}: for every fixed $p\in(0,1)\backslash\{\frac12\}$, asymptotic normality holds if and only if the standardized third moment converges to zero. The more familiar {\it fourth moment condition}, which requires the standardized fourth moment to converge to $3$, gives an equivalent characterization except at the two exceptional probabilities $p=\frac{1\pm1/\sqrt3}{2}$. At these values, the standardized fourth moment converges to $3$ for every graph sequence with a diverging number of edges, even when Gaussian convergence fails. In contrast, in the balanced case $p=\frac12$, the fourth moment condition characterizes asymptotic normality, while the third moment condition is insufficient. These results identify three distinct regimes for moment characterizations of Gaussian convergence, determined by the coloring probability. We further show that the third moment condition remains sufficient in the sparse regime, where $p=p_n \to 0$. As an application, we derive the limiting null distribution of two-sample statistics based on undirected $K$-nearest-neighbor graphs in the Poissonized setting, identifying sharp growth conditions on $K$ for asymptotic normality.

title: Free energy and fluctuations of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models and generalized Hopfield models
abstract: We consider the free energy of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models in the high temperature regime, with one spin normalized and the other either normalized or i.i.d. We derive a unified formula for the limiting free energy in both settings. We also prove that the fluctuations of the free energy converge to a Gaussian distribution under mild assumptions. The proof is based on a bipartite multigraph expansion, which also gives free energy results for generalized Hopfield models and log likelihood ratio of spiked rectangular models.

title: Conditional Reflected Backward Stochastic Differential Equations
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new type of reflected backward stochastic differential equations (reflected BSDEs), referred to as conditional reflected BSDEs, in which the conditional expectation of the Y-component of the solution with respect to a given sub-σ-algebra appears in both the generator and the obstacle. Under a Lipschitz condition on the loss function with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution for both the case of Lipschitz generator and the case of quadratic generator, bounded terminal value and bounded loss function. When the generator has quadratic growth and the terminal value and loss function are unbounded, we establish the uniqueness with the help of θ-method. Finally, a penalization approximation scheme holds under an additional monotonicity structure imposed on the generator and the loss function, without any restriction on the Lipschitz constants of the loss function.

title: A first order phase transition for lower tails in sparse random graphs
abstract: We study the graphon variational problem that governs lower tail large deviations of the number of copies of a fixed nonbipartite graph $H$ in a sparse Erdős--Rényi random graph. Our main new insight is that any non-constant minimizer of the variational problem exhibits a discontinuous jump away from the constant graphon. We deduce that the replica-symmetric and symmetry-breaking regimes are separated by a single critical parameter and that the phase transition is first order. In the supercritical regime $p \gg n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, we transfer these results to the conditioned random graph, showing that the edge density is a discontinuous order parameter and that the conditioned graph concentrates in cut distance near the full minimizer set.

title: Nonparametric In-Context Learning and Inference via Measure-Indexed Kernel Ridge Regression
abstract: In-Context learning enables an estimator, trained across multiple tasks, to adapt to a new unseen task solely through its in-context samples, without any parameter refitting. Despite growing interest in the statistical foundations of in-context learning, two gaps still remain. First, existing convergence results do not characterize the distributional behavior of the in-context learning estimators. Second, classical nonparametric methods are not designed to handle the measure-valued inputs that in-context learning naturally produces. We address both gaps by developing a measure-indexed reproducing kernel Hilbert space framework, in which the adaptivity of the estimator is captured through the dependence of a mean functional on the empirical measure of the context. Within this framework, we propose a measure-indexed kernel ridge regression estimator computed from multiple independent tasks and establish its minimax-optimal convergence rate. We further prove that the proposed estimator is pointwise asymptotically normal, enabling the construction of confidence intervals for the mean and prediction intervals for the response on an unseen task. Notably, the estimator achieves valid uncertainty quantification without any refitting when adapting to a new task. As a special case, our framework recovers classical distributed nonparametric regression when all tasks share the same underlying function. The proposed framework is illustrated through a latent Gaussian process example.

title: Generalised Fluctuating Dynamic Density-Functional Theory: Derivation and Applications
abstract: Classical density-functional theory is a powerful theoretical framework for studying the equilibrium density distribution of complex many-body systems. The core of the framework is to bridge microscopic and macroscopic descriptions of fluids through a variational principle that minimises the system's free energy. For dynamical settings, dynamic DFT (DDFT) extends the equilibrium framework to capture the time evolution of an order parameter, typically density. However, DDFT is often insufficient for mesoscopic systems far from equilibrium where fluctuations become significant, necessitating a stochastic extension: fluctuating DDFT. Here we derive a generalised FDDFT from first principles starting from the microscopic Hamiltonian dynamics using coarse-graining techniques, including Zwanzig's projection operator method. The resulting FDDFT applies to arbitrary observable fields, where the dynamics are driven by a thermodynamic force expressed in terms of an entropy functional. The dynamics consist of reversible, dissipative, and stochastic contributions, each directly linked to the underlying microscopic dynamics via the Liouville operator, Green-Kubo relations, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. To highlight the difference in the level of description between DDFT and FDDFT, we demonstrate how further coarse-graining via averaging leads to a generalised DDFT, valid at the macroscale. To showcase the effectiveness and utility of the generalised FDDFT, we apply it to two prototypical fluid systems: colloidal and simple viscous fluids. In the former case, we utilise the new formalism to re-derive the recently found colloidal FDDFT. In the latter case, we rigorously recover the non-isothermal extension of the Landau-Lifshitz fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations, providing fundamental derivation of this well-known phenomenological model, enabling to clarify its underlying principles.

title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation à la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.
