title: Cohomology and Representation Theory for Lie Superalgebras
abstract: In this paper the authors describe two general frameworks for studying algebraic supergroup and Lie superalgebra representations. These encompass the well-known rational representations for a reductive algebraic group and the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}$ for semisimple Lie algebras. Many of the important developments will be surveyed and a blueprint for these new approaches will be provided. The existence of odd elements simply add an additional layer of difficulty. The authors prove that the calculation of the sheaf cohomology in the super setting for the rational category is equivalent to understanding the Lie superalgebra cohomology. This generalizes the well-known fact that the classical Bott-Borel-Weil theorem is equivalent to Kostant's theorem. Furthermore, for the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}^{\mathfrak p}$ where ${\mathfrak p}$ is a principal parabolic, the authors show that the characters of simple modules can be obtained by looking at natural generalizations of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials given by extensions between simple modules and costandard modules arising from the underlying costandardly stratified category.

title: Mixing time of the tranvection walk on $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$
abstract: We consider a Markov chain on $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$, the space of $n \times n$ matrices with determinant $1$ and entries in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, for $p$ a prime number. By way of a log-Sobolev inequality, we show the mixing time of this chain is at most of order $O(n^2p^2(\log n +\log \log p))$.

title: Classification of twisted Yangians as coideal subalgebras of Yangians
abstract: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an involution $ω$. We classify the homogeneous right coideal subalgebras of the Yangian of $\mathfrak g$ whose classical limit is the enveloping algebra of the twisted current algebra, embedded in the standard way, without assuming any formula for the coaction. For nontrivial $ω$, they form a family parametrized by a spectral parameter and an element of the center of the fixed-point subalgebra; for $ω=\mathrm{id}$, only a spectral parameter occurs. All members of the family are isomorphic as graded algebras, through explicit isomorphisms. In particular, the twisted Yangians with a central correction introduced by Huang and Lu are coideal quantizations, and the $\imath$Yangian of quasi-split type $\mathsf A_{2n}$ is isomorphic to the traditional twisted Yangian studied by MacKay and by Belliard and Regelskis. The PBW property is proved uniformly from the classical affine Serre relations, without quantum defining relations. We also recover finite presentations in split and quasi-split types and verify the technical hypotheses of the quantum duality principle used by Lu, Wang, and Weekes.

title: Asymptotics of Weighted Bergman Polynomials under Finite Regularity
abstract: We study strong asymptotics of planar orthogonal polynomials with respect to fixed weighted area measures on Jordan domains. The aim is to understand how the regularity of the domain and the weight enter the large-degree asymptotic behavior of these polynomials. For domains with real-analytic boundaries, Suetin established leading-order asymptotics for Hölder continuous weights, while Hedenmalm--Wennman obtained a full asymptotic expansion for real-analytic weights. We interpolate between these results while allowing both the boundary and the weight to have finite smoothness. The resulting expansions have a length determined by the available regularity and hold in the exterior region and, under sufficient regularity conditions, in a shrinking neighborhood of the boundary.

title: Analytic quantum invariants
abstract: Using a deformed Borel-Laplace resummation, we propose a framework for repackaging quantum invariants as analytic invariants. We illustrate our approach through a detailed analysis of the coloured Jones polynomials of several simple knots, deriving explicit expressions for the resulting analytic invariants in terms of $(q,X)$-series. These invariants are closely related to, but generally distinct from, those obtained via the conventional Borel resummation of the Melvin-Morton-Rozansky expansion. As a further example, we construct an analytic invariant from a sequence of two-variable polynomials conjectured to be the Links-Gould polynomials of the figure-eight knot, associated with the quantum superalgebras $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}(n|1))$. Finally, we apply our technique to $q$-series arising in the study of three-manifold invariants, revealing connections with mock modular forms.

title: Singular Stochastic Heat Equations with Fractional Memory
abstract: We extend the paracontrolled distribution approach of Gubinelli, Imkeller, and Perkowski to singular stochastic heat equations with Caputo fractional time derivatives. By establishing Schauder estimates for the time-fractional heat flow and controlling history terms, we address the difficulties arising from temporal memory and the lack of the semigroup property. For the one-dimensional rough Burgers-type equation driven by space-time white noise with spatial dissipation \((-Δ)^σ\), we prove global well-posedness for \(σ\in(5/6,1]\) and \(ν\in(6σ/(12σ-5),1]\). For the heat equation with nonlinear multiplicative spatial white noise on the two-dimensional torus, we establish local well-posedness of renormalized solutions and an \(L^\infty\) blow-up criterion for every \(ν\in(0,1]\).

title: Ehrhart positivity for paving positroids
abstract: A central conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko, and Schröter posits that every positroid is Ehrhart positive. While Ehrhart positivity has recently been verified for notable classes such as lattice path matroids and series-parallel matroids, the general conjecture remains open. In this paper, we prove that the base polytope of any paving positroid has positive Ehrhart coefficients. This establishes a new class of Ehrhart positive positroids and provides substantial evidence supporting this conjecture.

title: Critical Free-Energy Variance in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
abstract: We study the variance of the free energy in the Gaussian Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at zero external field. For every system size and inverse temperature $β>0$, we prove $2N^2\operatorname{Var} F_N^{\mathrm{off}}(β) \le \logχ+(β^2-1)(χ-1), χ=N\mathbb{E}\langle R_{1,2}^2\rangle_β$, where $R_{1,2}$ is the replica overlap and $F_N^{\mathrm{off}}=N^{-1}\log Z_N^{\mathrm{off}}$ omits diagonal disorder. The proof uses an exact identity for the edges incident to one spin, Schur complements, and Gaussian disorder interpolation. At criticality the bound reduces to $2N^2\operatorname{Var} F_N^{\mathrm{off}}(1)\le\logχ$. An explicit nonnegative integral measures its gap. A second decomposition relates this gap to a mixed cubic overlap functional. Existing moment and cavity estimates imply that its required integral is bounded. Critical susceptibility asymptotics give the sharp logarithmic upper coefficient and show that the gap converges exactly when the variance has a constant term. We extend an entropy bound throughout bounded critical temperature windows and establish overlap moment stability on a smaller interval.

title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
abstract: Consider the bipartite Erdős--Rényi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $γ= n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Marčenko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $γ$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values. Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.

title: Distribution Functions and Moments of Harmonically Trapped Inertial Run-and-Tumble Particles in a Shear-Thickening Medium
abstract: We study the dynamics of an athermal inertial active particle confined in a harmonic potential and moving through shear-thickening media in one dimension. The activity is modeled using a symmetric dichotomous noise of strength $Σ$ and flipping rate $λ$, which mimics a run-and-tumble particle. The shear-thickening response of the medium is incorporated through a velocity-dependent viscous force of the form $g(v) \sim \tan(v)$. Starting from the Fokker-Planck equations corresponding to the particle's dynamics, we numerically compute the time-dependent joint probability density function $f(x,v,t)$ using a finite-volume upwind scheme. Next, we numerically solve the particle's equations of motion to obtain the steady-state position $P_s(x)$ and velocity $W_s(v)$ distributions and compare them with the marginal distributions obtained from $f(x,v,t)$ at sufficiently large $t$. The two approaches show excellent agreement. Both $P_s(x)$ and $W_s(v)$ exhibit several intriguing transitions as $λ$ is varied, and they eventually approach Gaussian-like profiles at sufficiently large $λ$. Our study of the time-dependent position-velocity correlation, $\langle xv \rangle(t)$, shows that larger values of $λ$ lead to faster relaxation to the steady state when all other parameters are held constant.

title: Coefficient lifting for skew divided differences and triple Schubert coefficients
abstract: Skew divided difference operators \(\partial_{w/v}\), introduced by Macdonald, play an important role in the study of Schubert polynomials and their structure constants. For permutations \(u,v,w\in S_n\), we show that the coefficient of each monomial \(\xx^α\) in \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\), where \(\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\) is the double Schubert polynomial, is a single triple Schubert coefficient evaluated at \(\tb=0\), whose indices form an explicit lift of \((u,v,w)\) to \(S_{n+\absα}\). As an application, we show that every coefficient of \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx)\) is a single Schubert structure constant. This gives a new proof of Kirillov's conjecture that these coefficients are nonnegative.

title: A universal framework for Hopf algebras in combinatorics
abstract: A universal framework for Hopf algebras in combinatorics provides a unified understanding of combinatorial objects. To establish such a framework, we dualize the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras developed by Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile, obtaining the category of rooted Hopf algebras. An object in this category is a graded connected Hopf algebra equipped with a group-like element, called a root, in its completion. These roots dualize the character theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras and provide a natural way to extend Bernstein and raising operators to other rooted Hopf algebras. The resulting constructions extend Schur, Hall--Littlewood, and Macdonald functions to rooted Hopf algebras. As an application, we develop these constructions for symmetric functions in noncommuting variables.

title: A logarithmic Brascamp--Lieb variance inequality
abstract: We prove a strengthened Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even log-concave measures whose positive sublevel bodies satisfy the local logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequality. The conclusion can be written either by adding a rank-one term to the Hessian of the potential or by adding an explicit nonnegative remainder to the variance. The proof uses sublevel volume variations, a one-dimensional Brascamp--Lieb inequality, and the coarea formula. The derivative of the potential under dilations gives an equality function whenever it is square-integrable. For potentials homogeneous of degree greater than one, we obtain a sharp radial remainder.

title: Hydrodynamic limits of finite range exclusion processes
abstract: We consider variants of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) where particles are 'large'; while in the SSEP, each lattice point is either occupied or not occupied by a single particle, in our model each particle is represented by a fixed shape, and the dynamics is so that shapes cannot overlap. In one dimension, this reduces to a finite range interaction that prevents particles from coming closer to each other than a certain distance. In this case, we prove the existence of the hydrodynamic limit, and identify the relevant macroscopic PDE, which is a porous medium equation. In two dimensions, we have no rigorous results, but instead rely on numerical simulations to approximate the diffusion matrix. Under the assumption that the hydrodynamic limit exists in two dimensions, we derive properties of the diffusion matrix based on the shape of the particles.

title: Integral forms for Yangians of classical type
abstract: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a simple Lie algebra of classical type. We construct a $\mathbb Z[1/2]$-integral form of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak g)$ generated by divided powers of the positive and negative Drinfeld generators, and establish its triangular decomposition and PBW basis. Under the loop filtration, its associated graded algebra is the current algebra part of Garland's integral form. As applications, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>3$, we identify the small Yangian with the restricted Yangian and classify their finite dimensional simple modules in terms of restricted Drinfeld polynomials.

title: Maximum likelihood, neural networks and posterior mean for inferring fractional Brownian motion parameters
abstract: Fractional Brownian motion (fBM) is a model of anomalous diffusion parameterised by a Hurst exponent $H \in (0,1)$ and a generalised diffusion coefficient $D_H > 0$. We jointly estimate $H$ and $D_H$ using maximum likelihood (MLE) from density measurements with Poisson counting noise and single-particle trajectory with Gaussian localisation error. We show that one density measurement in time cannot infer both $H$ and $D_H$ and that several time points are needed, which matters most for inference precision. For trajectories, we show that a neural network trained with a squared error loss approximates the posterior mean of $H$, which can be computed exactly at negligible cost. Paired with the profile-likelihood estimate of $D_H$, the posterior mean has the lowest root mean squared error in both $H$ and $D_H$, except near $H=0$ and $H=1$ where MLE estimates $H$ better. In vesicle trajectories from two cell types, $H$ and $D_H$ form a continuum rather than distinct modes of motion. The posterior probability that each window within a track is subdiffusive or superdiffusive shows that $26\%$ of MRC5 fibroblast and $21\%$ of HeLa vesicle trajectories contain both subdiffusive and superdiffusive windows, against $2\%$ and $7\%$ expected from estimation uncertainty alone. Intracellular cargoes therefore switch between subdiffusion and superdiffusion over time rather than forming populations with fixed $H$.

title: Fluctuations in the Potts spin glass model at high temperature
abstract: We study the fluctuations of the free energy of the Potts spin glass with $κ$ colors at high temperature. The disorder is symmetric with unit variance and finite fourth moment. For configurations with a balanced, or nearly balanced, color profile, the log-partition function satisfies a central limit theorem whenever $β^2<α_c(κ)$. Here $κα_c(κ)$ is the critical inverse temperature of the Curie-Weiss-Potts model. A comparison of color profiles transfers this limit to the unconstrained model for $β<β_{\max}(κ)$, an explicit threshold. In the same range, the magnetizations of two replicas and their overlap matrix satisfy a joint quenched central limit theorem with independent Gaussian limits. The fourth cumulant of the disorder enters the limiting mean and variance explicitly.

title: Local Linearization and Exact Oscillations for the Nonlinear Stochastic Heat Equation with Spatially Rough Noise
abstract: Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear stochastic heat equation $$ \frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial^2 u(t,x)}{\partial x^2} + σ(u(t,x))\dot W(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb R, $$ where $\dot W$ is a Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1/2)$. Hu et al. ({\it Ann. Probab.} {\bf 45} (2017), 4561--4616) established existence and uniqueness of the solution under the assumptions that $σ$ is differentiable, both $σ$ and $σ'$ are Lipschitz continuous, and $σ(0)=0$. Hu and Wang ({\it Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat.} {\bf 58} (2022), 379--423) subsequently removed the technical condition $σ(0)=0$ by developing the well-posedness theory in a suitable weighted space associated with the weight $λ(x)= c_H (1 + |x|^2)^{H-1}$. In this weighted framework, which allows $σ(0)\ne0$, we establish temporal and spatial local linearizations: small increments of the nonlinear solution are approximated by the corresponding increments of the solution to the additive equation, multiplied by the local coefficient $σ(u(t,x))$. The main difficulty lies in handling the nonlocal fractional-difference structure induced by the rough spatial noise. We address this difficulty using weighted heat-kernel increment estimates. These approximations yield exact Lévy-type uniform moduli of continuity in both time and space, together with Khinchin and Chung laws of the iterated logarithm.

title: Intermittency for the parabolic Anderson model on spaces with sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates
abstract: We study the parabolic Anderson model $\partial_t u=Δu+βu\,\dot W_α$ on an unbounded Ahlfors $d_h$-regular Dirichlet metric measure space whose heat kernel satisfies two-sided sub-Gaussian estimates with walk dimension $d_w$. The noise is white in time and, in space, either white ($α=0$) or colored through the Riesz kernel of $(-Δ)^{-2α}$, where $0\le 2α<d_h/d_w<1+2α$. No recurrence is assumed. We prove existence, uniqueness and Hölder regularity of the mild Skorohod solution for bounded initial conditions. For nonzero nonnegative bounded initial conditions, the solution is positive and its moment Lyapunov exponents exist for every real $p\ge1$, independently of the spatial point and the initial condition. For $p\ge2$, these exponents have order $p\,(β^2(p-1))^{d_w/((1+2α)d_w-d_h)}$, with upper and lower bounds matching up to constants.

title: Stochastic Gradient Descent: A Nonlinear Time Series Perspective
abstract: This paper investigates the statistical behavior of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with constant step size under the framework of iterated random functions. Compared to previous studies establishing the convergence of SGD in probability measure, e.g., Wasserstein distance, our approach directly provides the convergence in Euclidean distance by showing the Geometric Moment Contraction (GMC) of SGD. This new convergence can address the non-stationarity of SGD due to fixed initial points and can provide a more refined asymptotic analysis of SGD. Specifically, we prove quenched central limit theorem, invariance principle and $α$-stable convergence for averaged SGD (ASGD) regardless of initialization. Furthermore, we provide a novel perspective to understand the impact of step sizes in SGD by studying its derivative with respect to the step size. The existence of stationary solutions for the derivative processes is shown, enabling the use of interpolation to recover the full-trajectory of SGD. Subsequently, we utilize multiple step sizes and show an enhanced Richardson-Romberg extrapolation with improved bias representation, which brings ASGD estimates closer to the global optimum. Finally, we propose a new online inference method and a bias-reduced variant for the extrapolated ASGD. Empirical confidence intervals are constructed and the coverage probabilities approach the nominal level as $n$ grows.

title: Macroscopic fluctuation theory of stochastic systems undergoing monitoring
abstract: We develop a macroscopic fluctuation theory for diffusive classical lattice gases subject to continuous coarse-grained monitoring. Treating measurements in the typical-outcome (quenched) regime, we show that observation adds a quadratic confining term to the MFT action that pins the density to its hydrodynamic profile. We derive sufficient conditions under which, in the presence of monitoring, the current large-deviation function remains convex, the additivity principle holds, and dynamical phase transitions are excluded. For particle-hole-symmetric one-dimensional models we find that monitoring suppresses dynamical phase transitions and can change their order from second to first, as we demonstrate in the Katz--Lebowitz--Spohn model. In the strong-measurement limit, we find that the current distribution becomes Gaussian and determine the scaling of its cumulants: they follow simple power laws when the mobility remains nonzero throughout the system, but exhibit anomalous logarithmic scaling when the mobility vanishes at the boundaries.

title: Proof of a nonnegativity conjecture of Prellberg--Stanton
abstract: In 1994, Friedman, Joichi and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $q+(1-q)\prod_{i=n}^{2n-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i}}$ are nonnegative for $n\geq3$ and $n$ being odd. Let $\qbinom nm$ denote the Gaussian polynomial. In 2003, Prellberg and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $(1-q)\qbinom nm\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i+m}}$ are nonnegative for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. The latter conjecture implies the former. In this paper, we prove a stronger result concerning coefficientwise nonnegativity of another power series, which implies the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton. The proof uses a Möbius correction from Gaussian polynomials, weight-preserving injections on partitions, explicit linearly independent vectors in the kernel of a derivation operator and the KOH identity.

title: The nabla operator, Hall--Littlewood polynomials and LLT polynomials
abstract:
Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler conjectured that $(-1)^{n-\ell(μ)}
abla\widetilde H_μ[X;0,t]$ and $
ablaω\widetilde H_μ[X;0,t^{-1}]$ are Schur positive, and that $
ablaω\widetilde H_μ[X;0,t^{-1}]-
ablaω\widetilde H_ν[X;0,t^{-1}]$ is Schur positive when $μ$ dominates $ν$. The first statement follows from the compositional shuffle conjecture of Haglund, Morse, and Zabrocki, proved by Carlsson and Mellit. We prove the other two statements. All three statements also hold for $
abla^r$ with $r\geq1$. The main new step is an identity: when $μ$ covers $ν$, the difference $ω\widetilde H_μ[X;0,t^{-1}]-ω\widetilde H_ν[X;0,t^{-1}]$ is minus a power of $t$ times one LLT polynomial. Using the Catalanimals and the Cauchy identity of Blasiak, Haiman, Morse, Pun, and Seelinger, we show that $
abla^r$ of this LLT polynomial is, up to sign, a positive sum of LLT polynomials. We also extend the main results to the Schiffmann algebra setting.

title: Very high genus double Hurwitz numbers via mixing times
abstract: We obtain very high genus asymptotics for double Hurwitz numbers when both the size $n$ and the genus $g$ go to infinity, under the constraint that $g$ grows much faster than $n$, more precisely that $\frac{2g}{n}-\ln n\to\infty$. Our proof relies on adapting arguments about the mixing time of the transposition random walk introduced by Diaconis and Shahshahani.

title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.

title: Connectivity and Diameter of Friends and Strangers Graphs Using Minimum Degree
abstract: Given graphs $X,Y$ on $n$ vertices, Defant and Kravitz defined the friends and strangers graph, denoted $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$. The vertices of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ are bijections $σ:V(X)\to V(Y)$, and two bijections $σ$ and $σ'$ are adjacent in $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ if they differ by a transposition $(ab)$ such that $a$ and $b$ are adjacent in $X$ and $σ(a)$ and $σ(b)$ are adjacent in $Y$. Our main result resolves a conjecture of Bangachev that if $X,Y$ are connected graphs and $2\min\{δ(X),δ(Y)\}+3\max\{δ(X),δ(Y)\}\ge 3n$, then $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is connected. The main step in the proof is showing that there exists an absolute constant $C$ such that for any adjacent vertices $a,b\in V(X)$ and any vertex $σ\in V(\mathrm{FS}(X,Y))$, $a$ and $b$ can swap positions in at most $C$ moves. Furthermore, we prove that if $X,Y$ are connected graphs satisfying the above minimum degree condition, then the diameter of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is $O(n^2/\min\{δ(X),δ(Y)\})$, and that this is sharp as a bound on the maximum diameter of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ in this regime. This work improves the diameter results of Akella and Li, and resolves many of their questions. Moreover, we show that even for disconnected graphs $X$ and $Y$, the same minimum degree condition implies that the diameter of any connected component of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is $O(n^2)$.

title: Uniform-in-Time and Uniform-in-Temperature Particle Approximations of Coulomb MMD Flows
abstract: We study particle approximations of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) flows with the Coulomb kernel on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d\ge2$, driven by thermal noise of strength $τ\ge0$. For smooth, strictly positive initial and target densities and i.i.d. initial positions, we prove that the expected Wasserstein-1 distance between the empirical measure and the mean-field solution is at most of order $N^{-1/d}$ for $d\ge3$ and $\sqrt{(\log N)/N}$ for $d=2$, uniformly in time and in the temperature $τ\ge0$, including the deterministic case $τ=0$. At each fixed $τ>0$, we also prove propagation of chaos in total variation for any $k$-fold marginal distributions of particles, uniformly in time, with a bound of order $\sqrt{k/τ}$ times the empirical convergence rate. Our proof uses the modulated free-energy method of Bresch, Jabin, and Wang to reduce the particle convergence estimate to a relaxation estimate that controls the time integral of the mean-field velocity gradient uniformly in $τ\ge0$. Near zero temperature, where the smoothing effect of the noise degenerates, we obtain this estimate by recentering the dynamics at thermal equilibrium and using the damping generated by the Coulomb interaction.

title: Maximum degree for random geometric graphs in the connectivity regime and beyond
abstract: A random geometric graph is a random graph model whose vertex set is a binomial point process, where two vertices are connected by an edge if each lies within the ball of radius $r$ centered at the other. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic fluctuations of the threshold radius required for the maximum degree of the graph to reach a target value. Assuming this target value grows with the number of vertices $n$ at an order of at least $\log n$ but strictly less than $(\log n)^d$, we show that these fluctuations follow a Gumbel distribution. We also investigate the spatial configurations of vertices with extremely large degrees, and show that the point process marked by their degrees converges in distribution to a Poisson point process.

title: Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties
abstract: Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved. We obtain an explicit formula for the point-counting polynomials of their open parts in terms of increasing minimal weight paths, extending Dyer's formula for Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials. Over the real numbers, their totally nonnegative parts are regular CW complexes homeomorphic to closed balls, which gives a natural geometric realization of the posets of tilted Bruhat subintervals in all Lie types. Over the complex numbers, we prove that their fundamental classes push forward under a continuous loop evaluation map to the Poincaré duals of the minimal-degree coefficients of quantum Schubert products.

title: Upper tail large deviation for the first passage time in the frog model on $Z^d$ with $d\geq 2$
abstract: We study upper tail large deviations for the first passage time in the frog model on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge 2$. Let $\mathrm{T}(0,x)$ denote the first time at which the infection, started from the origin, reaches $x$, and let $μ$ be the associated time constant. We prove that, for any Euclidean unit vector $v\in\mathbb R^d$ and $ξ>0$, \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} -\frac{1}{\mathfrak{s}_d(n)} \log \mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{T}(0,\lfloor nv\rfloor) \ge (μ(v)+ξ)n\bigr) =\mathfrak{r}_dξ, \] where $\mathfrak s_2(n)=n/\log n$ and $\mathfrak r_2=π$ for $d=2$; $\mathfrak s_d(n)=n$ and $\mathfrak r_d$ is the escape probability of simple random walk for $d\ge3$. Moreover, on the upper tail large deviation event, we show that a certain slowdown mechanism occurs near the endpoint. To rule out other mechanisms, we analyze the growth of the infection near the starting point using a modified exploration process, and investigate its propagation through the intermediate region using the renormalization and covering arguments.

title: Statistical inference for rough Burgers-type stochastic partial differential equations
authors: Simon Chony Acosta Christian Olivera Ciprian Tudor
abstract: We consider the Burgers-type stochastic PDE \[ du = θ\,\partial_x^2 u\,dt + f(u)\,dt + g(u)\,\partial_x u\,dt + σ\,dW(t), \] driven by space--time white noise on the one-dimensional torus, where \(θ>0\) is the diffusivity parameter and \(σ>0\) the noise intensity. The transport term \(g(u)\,\partial_x u\) admits no classical interpretation, and we work with the mild solutions defined via rough paths following~\cite{Hairer2011}, for which the solution decomposes as \(u=ψ+R\) with \(ψ\) a stationary centred Gaussian process solving a damped stochastic heat equation and \(R\) a remainder. We first show that, away from the initial time, \(R\) is Lipschitz in space and Hölder in time of order strictly greater than \(1/2\), hence strictly smoother than \(ψ\) in both variables. We then compute exactly the spatial quadratic variation and the temporal quartic variation of \(ψ\), almost surely and not merely in \(L^{2}(Ω)\), and prove that the corresponding variations of \(u\) are unaffected by the remainder. Combined with an exact time-scaling identity, this separation of regularity scales yields strongly consistent pathwise estimators of \(θ\). title: A positivity conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton
abstract: We prove the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton (2003) that $\frac{1-q}{(q^n;q)_m}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}$ has nonnegative power-series coefficients for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. An extension of this bound proves the Reiner--Stanton--White conjecture on positivity of orbit polynomials for flags of subspaces.

title: Random walk in a regenerating random environment
abstract: In this paper we consider random walks moving in a dynamic random environment that is completely resampled with probability $p$ after each step of the random walker. This resampling yields a straightforward regeneration structure and limit theorems, such as a law of large numbers with a limiting speed $v(p)$ that depends on $p$. We investigate several properties of $v(p)$ as a function of $p$, such as differentiability and monotonicity. Similarily, we study the limiting diffusivity $σ^2(p)$ in a central limit theorem.

title: First-order $Γ$-expansion for entropic optimal transport with non-degenerate costs
abstract: Entropy-regularized optimal transport (EOT) has become a key tool in optimal transport, providing both theoretical insight and efficient computation via the Sinkhorn algorithm. We study the first-order \(Γ\)-expansion of EOT as the regularization parameter \(\varepsilon\) vanishes, by rewriting EOT as the minimization of a relative entropy with respect to a Gibbs measure \(\gibbs\) associated with the duality gap energy. Using a mild extension of the Laplace method, we prove the convergence of the Gibbs measures and derive this \(Γ\)-expansion for non-degenerate ground costs, under suitable assumptions on the duality gap, the contact set and the marginals. This yields at the same time an entropic selection principle and an expansion of the EOT cost up to \(o(\varepsilon)\) for this class of ground costs, generalizing existing results.

title: A method for generating multivariate multiple orthogonal polynomials
abstract: In the framework of multiple orthogonal polynomials (MOPs) and their extension to the multivariate setting, a unified mechanism for generating structured families of multiple orthogonal polynomials across diverse multidimensional domains is still lacking. In this work, we bridge this gap by developing an extended Koornwinder-type methodology for constructing multivariate multiple orthogonal polynomials. We introduce two distinct coupling schemes: combining a univariate MOPs family with a standard orthogonal family, which enables the definition of both Type I and Type II bivariate systems along with their dual biorthogonality relations, and coupling two univariate MOPs families to form Type II multivariate systems. Using this general framework, we provide the first explicit formulations of multiple orthogonal polynomials on a variety of bivariate regions, including bounded domains such as a parabolic domain and the square $[0,1]^2$, non-standard unbounded geometries like the positive quadrant $(\mathbb{R}_0^+)^2$ and the wedge $\mathbb{V}^2$, as well as new constructions on the triangle $T$. Furthermore, explicit multiple orthogonal systems on the $d$-dimensional simplex $T^d$ and on the $d$-dimensional cone $\mathbb{V}^d$ are given.

title: The singularity probability of dense random regular graphs
abstract: Let $G_{n,d}$ be a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, and let $A_n$ be its adjacency matrix. For every fixed $λ\in(0,1/2)$, we prove that for any $λ(n-1)\le d\le(1-λ)(n-1)$, $\mathbb P(A_n\text{ is singular})\le e^{-cn}$, where $c>0$ depends only on $λ$, and $n$ is sufficiently large with $nd$ even.

title: Mixing Times of Switch Chains via High-Dimensional Expansion
abstract: The switch chain is a Markov chain defined on the set of labelled realizations of a given graphical degree sequence. At each step, a pair of vertex-disjoint edges is chosen at random and the process attempts to replace them with a uniformly chosen perfect matching of the same four vertices, rejecting any proposal that would create a multiple edge. The resulting process is reversible with respect to the uniform distribution on all realizations. We investigate the mixing time of this chain by viewing realizations as the facets of a simplicial complex and studying a variant of the original process called the simplicial switch chain, which we analyze using tools from the theory of high-dimensional expansion. Our technical contributions include a proof that links of faces of sufficiently high codimension are strong spectral expanders and a comparison between the Dirichlet energies of large block updates and two-edge updates. Our main result is an $O(Δ^{2}m\log m)$ bound on the mixing time of both simplicial and classical switch chains whenever $m\ge CΔ^{8}$, where $m$ is the number of edges, $Δ$ is the maximum prescribed degree, and $C>0$ is an absolute constant. For sequences on $n$ vertices with fixed maximum degree, this proves that the chain mixes in $O(n\log n)$ steps, resolving a longstanding conjecture of Cooper, Dyer, and Greenhill and extending its conclusion to irregular degree sequences.

title: Monotone Multiple Stopping and Last-Success Problems
abstract: An optimal stopping problem is monotone when its stopping region is preserved under subsequent transitions, so that the one-step look-ahead stopping time is optimal. We develop a finite-horizon discrete-time theory of multiple stopping that separates general recursive dynamic programming from this stronger monotone structure. Extending the classical martingale-system approach, we construct a recursively defined optimal vector of stopping times without assuming monotonicity. If monotonicity holds at every exercise level, this vector coincides with the recursive vector of one-step look-ahead stopping times. A bounded counterexample shows that monotonicity of the original single-stopping problem alone is insufficient, whereas monotonicity propagates to every level when the level-one one-step look-ahead function is deterministic. We apply the theory to multiple-selection last-success problems. For the classical independent odds setting, a continuous-time Poisson embedding gives an alternative proof of the multiple-stopping lower bound and clarifies the associated threshold constants. We also examine random horizons, Markov-dependent trials, and an unknown success probability

title: Limit theorems for one-dimensional diffusions: reflected, skew, sticky, skew-sticky, and snapping-out limits
abstract: We establish general conditions for the weak convergence of regular one-dimensional diffusion processes when their scale functions, speed measures, state spaces and boundary conditions may substantially vary. Our approach is based on the classical Itô--McKean representation of regular diffusions via time changes and scale transformations of a single Brownian motion. This reduces many stochastic convergence problems to deterministic questions concerning the convergence of integrals, monotone functions, compositions, and generalized inverses. As a main application, we investigate various homogenization regimes for diffusions in media with closely spaced semipermeable membranes, where the resulting limiting processes include not only reflected and skew Brownian motions, but also skew-sticky Brownian motions and snapping-out diffusions. This yields a representation of a snapping-out diffusion as a function of a single Brownian motion, without introducing an auxiliary sequence of independent exponential random variables.

title: Conformal invariance of the planar four-state Potts model and its random-cluster representation
abstract: For the critical random-cluster model on $\mathbb Z^2$ with cluster-weight $q=4$, we prove the convergence of loops to CLE(4) in the scaling limit. Conformal invariance of the four-state Potts model is then deduced via the Edwards-Sokal coupling.

title: Long-Range Nonequilibrium Correlations as a Thermodynamic Speedometer
abstract: Despite purely local microscopic dynamics, nonequilibrium steady states can develop long-range correlations. This bound is approached in the quasistatic limit, whereas progressively shorter-wavelength modes do not generally satisfy the corresponding bound. These results provide a quantitative connection between the curvature of the large-deviation functional, long-range correlations in the nonequilibrium steady state, and finite-time dissipation. Within the linear-response regime considered here, they indicate that the longest-wavelength hydrodynamic mode has a distinct relation between slow relaxation and thermodynamic irreversibility.

title: Electrical Networks and Symplectic Invariants
abstract: Consider a finite planar graph with positive real edge weights and designated boundary vertices, called nodes. Such a graph is called a circular planar electrical network. A grove is a spanning forest in which every component contains at least one node. The connected components of a grove determine a partition of the nodes. We relate weighted grove counts to invariant theory for the symplectic group. To a planar electrical network $G$, we associate an $\mathrm{Sp}(2n)$-invariant tensor $Z_G$. For $\mathrm{Sp}(2)=\mathrm{SL}(2)$, we expand $Z_G$ in the Temperley--Lieb basis indexed by noncrossing matchings and relate its coefficients to the Kenyon--Wilson grove formulas. For $\mathrm{Sp}(4)$, we give reduction rules for superpositions of two groves and prove that the tensors indexed by $3$-noncrossing matchings form a basis of the space of $\mathrm{Sp}(4)$-invariant tensors. The coefficients of $Z_G$ in this basis are weighted counts of reduced double groves, up to normalization.

title: The stochastic fractional transport heat equation
abstract: We give an introduction to the time-fractional stochastic heat equation driven by 1+d-parameter fractional time-space white noise, in the following two cases: (i) With additive fractional time-space white noise (ii) With multiplicative time-space Brownian noise The fractional time derivative is interpreted as the Caputo derivative of order $α\in (0,2]$ and we assume that the Hurst coefficient $H=(H_0,H_1,H_2, ...,H_d)$ of the time-space fractional white noise is in $(\tfrac{1}{2},1)^{1+d}$. We find an explicit expression for the unique solution in the sense of distribution of the equation in the additive noise case (i). In the multiplicative case (ii) we derive the correct space--time convolution equation and its Wiener chaos expansion. For $1<α\leq2$ a second initial condition is required. The endpoint $α=2$ is treated separately and yields a stochastic wave equation with finite propagation speed. A solution $Y(t,x)$ is called \emph{mild} if $E[Y^2(t,x)] < \infty$ for all $t,x$. In the multiplicative case the random-field condition is expressed by the square integrability of the forcing kernel. For the classical Laplacian and space--time white noise, the endpoint $α=2$ admits a random-field solution only in space dimension $d=1$. This paper is partly a survey paper, explaining the concepts and methods behind the results. It is also partly a research paper, in the sense that some results are new, to the best of our knowledge.

title: Staircase phase transitions for the largest eigenvalue of heavy-tailed sample correlation matrices
abstract: We establish staircase phase transitions for the largest eigenvalue of heavy-tailed sample correlation matrices formed from a $p_n \times n$ data matrix with i.i.d. real entries of mean zero and unit variance, allowing an infinite fourth moment. In the proportional regime $p_n / n \to ϕ\in (0, \infty)$, the first-order asymptotics depend jointly on the aspect ratio and the entry tail. The transitions are driven by collisions of large entries in distinct rows of a common column. The first collision order capable of producing a separated upper outlier is $k_* (ϕ) = \lfloor \sqrtϕ \rfloor + 2$, yielding the critical tail exponent $α_* (ϕ) = 2 + 2 / k_* (ϕ)$. This exponent decreases in steps as $ϕ$ increases, creating a staircase boundary between convergence to the upper Marčenko--Pastur edge and successive outlier levels. At exact critical tail scales, the point process of eigenvalues above the upper edge or the preceding deterministic level converges to a Poisson point process. The resulting nondegenerate limiting laws for the largest eigenvalue connect adjacent phases and have a positive atom at this baseline. If every fixed collision order is supercritical, the largest eigenvalue diverges in probability despite finite entry variance.

title: Finite-Sample Distribution Theory and Efficient Large-Scale Inference for Online Quantile Regression
abstract: This paper studies online quantile regression for large-scale and streaming data using Stochastic SubGradient Descent (SSGD) with constant learning rates. To bridge these gaps, we introduce new techniques to prove a quenched central limit theorem (CLT) and finite-sample Gaussian approximation for SSGD under a finite-moment assumption. We further show that Ruppert-Polyak averaging with a constant learning rate has a non-vanishing bias and fails to satisfy CLT centering at the population target. Hence we propose suffix averaging to address this issue and establish its finite-sample Gaussian approximation. Based on these results, we provide an efficient online inference method for quantile regression that avoids covariance estimation. Numerical experiments show that our method achieves desirable empirical coverage rates and competitive performance compared to other inference methods. We also apply our approach to U.S. wage data to demonstrate its practical effectiveness.

title: Stochastic heat equations with non-Lipschitz coefficients driven by symmetric $α$-stable Lévy white noise

We also construct a predictable mild solution on the same stochastic basis and with the same noise. At each fixed deterministic time, this mild solution is a density of the distribution-valued weak solution.

title: Central limit theorems for stochastic heat equation driven by Gaussian noise with heat-kernel covariance
abstract: In this article, we study the spatial fluctuations of the Skorohod solution to a stochastic heat equation on $\mathbb R^d$ for $d<4$, driven by multiplicative Gaussian noise with the non-separable covariance kernel $p_{|t-s|}(x-y)$. title: Gaussian fluctuations of differential observables of stationary lattice fields
abstract: We study Gaussian fluctuations of differential observables of centered stationary random fields on the discrete $d$-dimensional torus of mesh $1/N$. Under suitable assumptions on the spectral scaling limit $γ$ of the covariance and the normalized cumulants of order $r\geq3$, we prove convergence in law in a negative Sobolev space to a centered Gaussian random distribution with covariance multiplier $|p(k)|^2γ(k)$. The two factors separate the effects of the operator and the field and, notably, differentiation can compensate a low-frequency spectral singularity. For the lattice Gaussian Free Field, this gives a projected white-noise limit for the gradient. The proofs use Fourier analysis and the method of moments and cumulants, together with a tightness argument. title: Signed seeds and G-gradings on cluster algebras
abstract: The theory of cluster algebras is closely connected to the theory of total positivity; indeed, the desire to better understand total positivity was one of the main motivations for Fomin and Zelevinsky's introduction of cluster algebras [arXiv:math/0104151]. In particular, any cluster variety whose coordinate ring has a cluster structure has a natural notion of positive part: the subset of the variety where all cluster variables are positive. In this paper, we explain that there are other signed cells contained in cluster varieties that are equally natural from a cluster-theoretic point of view. These come from signed seeds, which can be thought of as a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-grading on cluster variables, and which were introduced in [arXiv:2310.17727] in the context of the amplituhedron. More generally, given any abelian group $G$, we introduce the notion of a $G$-graded seed for a cluster algebra, which is a way of assigning elements of $G$ to each cluster variable which is compatible with the cluster structure. When $G$ is the multiplicative group $\{-1, 1\}$, this recovers the above notion of signed seed; when $G = \mathbb{C}^*$, this recovers the notion of cluster automorphism group [GSV10] or cluster dilation group [arXiv:2603.17890]; and when $G = \mathbb{Z}^d$, this recovers the notion of graded cluster algebra studied by Grabowski-Launois [arXiv:1301.2133], Grabowski [arXiv:1309.6170] and Gekhtman-Shapiro-Vainshtein [GSV10, Section 5.2] (which had previously appeared in special cases in work of Fomin-Zelevinsky [arXiv:math/0602259]). The examples we study include the space of square matrices, symmetric matrices, skew-symmetric matrices, positroid varieties, and amplituhedron tiles. We also connect this notion to tropical mutation when $G = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Branching Gaps, Coexistence, and Boundary Influence for the Ising Model on Spherically Symmetric Trees
abstract: In this paper, we study the ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor Ising model on rooted spherically symmetric trees with one or \(q\) children per vertex, according to a prescribed sequence of branching levels. Conversely, uniqueness need not entail any uniform rate: for each prescribed vanishing sequence, we construct a density-one tree whose finite-volume boundary influence decays more slowly along a subsequence. The tree retains branching number \(q\), although its nonzero-field coexistence region disappears. For eventually bounded gaps, we prove an optimal uniform comparison with the periodic tree having the largest allowed gap and obtain an explicit interval of coexistence fields. Thus bounded gaps are equivalent, within this family, to coexistence at some finite temperature and nonzero field. For eventually periodic gaps, Gibbs uniqueness is equivalent to fixed-point uniqueness of the full-period return map. A negative Schwarzian derivative yields a complete classification: in the supercritical regime the map has three fixed points inside a closed coexistence interval, two at its endpoints, and one outside. The nonzero endpoints are automatically nondegenerate folds, with square-root splitting of the merging branches.

title: Partial identification with entropy regularized optimal transport
abstract: In many statistical settings, the available data and maintained assumptions do not suffice to uniquely identify the model parameters of interest. These are often characterized through linear programs that optimize over models compatible with the observed data. These programs can be infinite-dimensional in the optimizer and the number of constraints. We provide a unified way to characterize and solve such optimization problems by phrasing them as optimal transport problems on path spaces. This allows us to regularize the problem with an entropy penalty, recasting it as a multi-marginal entropic optimal transport problem, which can be solved efficiently via Sinkhorn iterations. In addition, it allows us to establish convergence of the regularized value to the sharpest bound, derive consistency rates for a plug-in estimator, and obtain asymptotic distribution for approximate bounds. The method is general and accommodates settings ranging from instrumental variable models with continuous variables to welfare estimation in heterogeneous demand models. title: Grassmannian tree webs and cluster variables
abstract: Homogeneous coordinate rings of Grassmannians are among the most fundamental instances of cluster algebras arising in ``nature.'' title: On the Spectrum of Some Temperley-Lieb Spin Chains

Furthermore, this value serves as a lower bound for the gap of the maximally mixed ground state. Finally, we show that the ground state projectors on open chains satisfy the Jones-Wenzl recursion, thereby recovering a known result that the degeneracies are the quantum integers $[L+1]_q$ for $q+q^{-1}=d$. title: Generalized Charlier Recurrence Coefficients: Hankel Formulas, Laguerre--Freud Dynamics, and Painlevé V Connections
abstract: We study the monic recurrence coefficients of the generalized Charlier polynomials associated with the discrete weight \[ ρ_μ(k) = \frac{μ^k}{(k!)^2}, \qquad k\in\mathbb N_0, \qquad μ>0. \] The coefficients $β_n$ and $γ_n$ in the recurrence relation \[ P_{n+1}(x) = (x-β_n)P_n(x)-γ_nP_{n-1}(x) \] are described through complementary moment, determinant, discrete dynamical, and continuous integrable formulations. We give a consistent normalization of the Markov function and its Jacobi continued fraction, and express the recurrence coefficients in terms of Hankel determinants, using a bordered determinant for the diagonal coefficient $β_n$. Starting from the original Laguerre--Freud equations, we derive the local recursive system used for computation and relate it to the Toda deformation. We also recall the known Painlevé~V representations associated with the two-parameter generalized Charlier family, in a normalization consistent with the present specialization. Moment/Hankelconstructions provide complementary moment-theoretic realizations of the recurrence coefficients, while the local Laguerre--Freud recursion provides an independent dynamical construction. Their comparison is used for numerical cross-validation. The numerical results are consistent with the leading large-degree behavior \[ β_n\sim n, \qquad γ_n\simμ. \]

title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $θ_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge θ_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $θ_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^β$, for any given $β\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $θ_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.

title: Moments of characteristic polynomials at random matrix Gram points
abstract: We evaluate the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix at the points on the unit circle where the polynomial takes real values. In analogy to the Riemann zeta function we call these the ``random matrix Gram points''. On the random matrix side we answer in the affirmative a question of Richard Hall, who expected that zeta on the Gram points should be larger than typical. We prove that for any fixed positive $k$, the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the random matrix Gram points is larger than the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the whole unit circle. For large $N$ the leading-order asymptotic term is the same size, but all lower-order terms are larger. In an appendix we show how to adapt the heuristic recipe of Conrey--Farmer--Keating--Rubinstein--Snaith to conjecture moments of zeta at Gram points, and show by example that the second and fourth moments calculated by following the recipe agree with previously proven results.

title: Convergence of a drainage network model with branching to the Brownian net
abstract: We consider a drainage network model represented by a system of coalescing random walks exhibiting long range dependence before coalescence. This model was introduced by Gangopadhyay et. al. [GRS04] and Coletti et. al. [CFD09] proved its convergence to the Brownian web under diffusive scaling. Santos et. al. [SVZ24] considered a branching version of this model where branching occurs with low probabilities varying with the scaling parameter and showed that any sub-sequential limit contains a copy of the Brownian net. It was conjectured that the limit is indeed the Brownian net. In this work we prove this conjecture. Further, compared to [SVZ24], we explore the question of scaling limit in a wider spectrum of scaling regime. This work contributes to the broader understanding of the basin of attraction of the Brownian net.

title: The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
abstract: Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.

title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
abstract: We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[θ_1,\ldots,θ_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$. We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.

title: Approximating the poles of a Painlevé V transcendent for the Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel
abstract: The Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel has an expression as an integral containing a Painlevé transcendent $r$ satisfying Painlevé V, in the same way that the Fredholm determinant of the Airy kernel has an expression involving the Hastings-McLeod solution of Painlevé II. In this paper we use Padé approximation to approximate the poles of this Painlevé transcendent $r$ in the complex plane. We use Padé approximation near $0$, Hermite-Padé approximation near $0$ and two-point Padé approximation near $0$ and infinity.

title: The smallest singular value of products of random combinatorial and deterministic matrices
abstract: Let $p\in(0,1/2]$ be fixed, and let $d,n$ be positive integers satisfying $d=pn$. Let $Q_n$ be an $n\times n$ random combinatorial matrix whose rows are independent and uniformly distributed over the vectors in $\{0,1\}^n$ having exactly $d$ ones. For an arbitrary deterministic invertible $n\times n$ matrix $M$, we establish two-sided bounds for the smallest singular value of $Q_nM$. More precisely, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left( \varepsilon\le s_n(Q_nM)\cdot \|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \le \varepsilon^{-2} \right) \ge 1-C\left( \varepsilon+d^{-1/2}+e^{-c\,\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})} \right)-2e^{-cn}, \] where positive constants $C, c$ depend only on $p$ and $\operatorname{sr}$ denotes the stable rank. Consequently, for any sequence of deterministic invertible matrices $M$ satisfying $\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})\to\infty$, $s_n(Q_nM)$ is typically of order $\|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{-1}$. In particular, taking $M=\mathbf I_n$ recovers the known $n^{-1/2}$ scale for $s_n(Q_n)$.

title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan 2-lift towers via Hilbert modular forms
abstract: Expander graphs have been central objects of study for over fifty years. Ramanujan graphs attain the asymptotically optimal nontrivial adjacency-eigenvalue threshold for infinite fixed-degree families. The original arithmetic constructions by Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak (1988) and Margulis (1988), and the iterative $2$-lift method of Bilu-Linial (2006) provide different approaches to Ramanujan graph constructions. Motivated by work on Mealy automata, we combine both approaches to give the following new arithmetic construction. For every prime $p\equiv 1\pmod {17}$, we construct a infinite tower of $(p+1)$-regular non-bipartite Ramanujan graphs on $2^n$ vertices, with label-preserving $2$-lifts between consecutive levels. These construction is strongly explicit: for fixed $p$, a neighbor or lift sign is computable in $O_p(n^3)$ bit operations. The construction uses fixed algebraic $2$-adic transformations, specified by finite data computable in preprocessing depending only on $p$. The main number-theoretic tool is Blasius's Ramanujan-Petersson theorem for Hilbert modular forms, applied through the Jacquet-Langlands correspondence to obtain the sharp bound $|λ|\leq2\sqrt p$ for every nontrivial adjacency eigenvalue of our $(p+1)$-regular graphs. The transformations preserve $2$-adic distance, which gives the binary covers and an explicit formula for their signings.

title: Optimal subtrees of finite metric graphs
abstract: We consider a metric graph analog of a classical extremal problem for Riemann surfaces studied by Teichmüller, Jenkins, Strebel, and others. In particular, we prove that on any finite metric graph with a marked point, there is a unique open subtree which maximizes a metric graph analog of the reduced modulus, and we also give an equivalent characterization of this optimal subtree in terms of balanced harmonic measures.

title: virasoro_blocks: Software for the 2d bootstrap
abstract: We introduce virasoro_blocks, software that computes Virasoro conformal blocks at any central charge in a form suitable for the numerical bootstrap. At each finite order in the elliptic nome, Zamolodchikov's recursion gives the block as a positive prefactor times a rational function of the exchanged weight. However, its many Kac poles make it difficult to use in semidefinite programming approaches to the bootstrap. In this software we use optimal interpolation to reduce the number of poles while keeping high accuracy. The software works in arbitrary precision and handles singular central charges, including the minimal models and $c=1$. It also computes global blocks, $N=1$ superconformal blocks, torus characters, and torus one-point blocks. We illustrate it with two applications. Assuming only scalar Virasoro primaries, we compute bounds on the scalar gap that approach the window of Liouville solutions between $(c-1)/16$ and $(c-1)/12$. We also bound the average exchanged dimension in four-point functions of identical scalars at several central charges. These bounds have a rich structure, and many known 2d CFTs lie on or near their boundary.

title: Entropic Fluctuations in Quantum Statistical Mechanics: A Review
abstract: The celebrated Evans--Searles, respectively Gallavotti--Cohen, fluctuation theorem concerns certain universal statistical features of the entropy production rate of a classical system in a transient, respectively steady, state. In this paper, we review and compare several possible extensions of these fluctuation theorems to quantum systems. We present, in an introductory way, the approach proposed in a recent series of works [Lett. Math. Phys. 114, 32 (2024): doi:10.1007/s11005-024-01777-0], [Rev. Math. Phys 38, 2461006 (2026): doi:10.1142/S0129055X24610063], [Commun. Math. Phys. 406, 201 (2025): 10.1007/s00220-025-05360-z] and [J. Math. Phys. 67, 022101 (2026): doi:10.1063/5.0311182] including a previously missing extension of the Gallavotti--Cohen (steady state) version of the FT to two-time measurement entropy production in the algebraic setting of quantum dynamical systems. We focus on the open quantum systems, where a small system interacts with several (infinitely extended) reservoirs, and discuss the following approaches: naive, two-time measurement, phase space contraction and ancilla state tomography. We review the connection with modular theory. The latter provides a way to extend the classical notions to the quantum domain. We discuss the quantum version of the principle of regular entropic fluctuations, introduced in the classical context in [Nonlinearity 24, 699 (2011): doi:10.1088/0951-7715/24/3/003]. Finally, we relate the statistical properties of these various notions of entropy production to spectral resonances of quantum transfer operators and apply this approach to a paradigmatic model of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: the spin-fermion model. The results presented here shed a new light on the nature of entropic fluctuations in quantum statistical mechanics.

title: The velocity is deterministic in random walk in 2-valued i.i.d. random environment
abstract: We prove that the limiting velocity for (nearest-neighbour) random walk in i.i.d. random environment is deterministic when the local environment is supported on two points. No ellipticity is assumed. The proof uses a clever adaption (suggested by ChatGPT) of coupling arguments previously developed by the authors. title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
abstract: We prove quantitative sub-ballisticity for the self-avoiding walk on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$. Namely, we obtain an explicit exponential rate of decay for the probability that a self-avoiding walk of length $n$ reaches distance at least $vn$, in terms of $v>0$. As a consequence, we show that the displacement of an $n$-step self-avoiding walk is at most $n/\exp(c\log^* n)$ with very high probability. Previously, only a non-quantitative $o(n)$ bound was known from the work of Duminil-Copin and Hammond. Along the way, we show that at criticality the partition function of bridges of length $n$ is on average bounded by $C/\log\log n$, which we believe to be of independent interest. Our approach is based on a quantitative analysis of the original nonconstructive proof of Duminil-Copin and Hammond using ideas from proof theory.

title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
abstract: We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.

title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
abstract: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper. As in earlier work, the proof proceeds by showing that all rank 3 Coxeter arrangements are clean arrangements, meaning that every biclosed set is weakly separated from its complement by a hyperplane. As a consequence, we also deduce Dyer's Conjecture A for all rank 3 Coxeter groups, which asserts that cover relations in extended weak order are given by toggling a single root.

title: Graftings and cograftings for species
abstract: We introduce graftings and cograftings for vector species, modelled on the elementary operations of adjoining and deleting a root in a rooted forest. We relate these maps to operads, up and down operators, and obtain nontrivial balanced pairs, admitting pair of creation/annihilation operators with commuting relations. Using Fock functors, we recover the classical Connes--Kreimer Hopf algebra, its noncommutative planar analogue, and Foissy's $q$-infinitesimal Hopf algebra.

title: Tracy Widom law for sample covariance matrices under quadratic form concentration
abstract: We study sample covariance matrices formed from i.i.d., centered, isotropic random vectors $q_1, \dots, q_N \in \mathbb{R}^M$, whose coordinates are allowed to be dependent. In particular, our result removes the unconditionality assumption in existing edge universality results for log-concave ensembles~\cite{BX}, resolving the question that originally motivated our work. The concentration assumption also allows us to extend the result beyond the log-concave class.

title: A Model for Fast Mining Blockchains
abstract: We study a Markovian model for a blockchain mining process. In the limit where there is an infinite number of miners, the model satisfies a functional law of large numbers due to Barbour and Luczac (2008), leading to an infinite set of coupled ODEs characterising the blockchain heights. We show that the sequence of solutions to this system converges uniformly, to a limiting profile in an appropriate comoving frame. Utilising asymptotic arguments inspired by Brunet and Derrida (1997), we derive an explicit expression for the position of the travelling front, which exhibits a leading order logarithmic Bramson correction in time. For a finite number of miners, we further derive a correction to the travelling speed which is logarithmic in the number of miners. Finally, by application of a computation due to Ablowitz and Zeppetella (1979), we identify that, for a specific choice of the travelling speed, the Painlevé integrable, travelling wave solution of the Fisher-KPP equation with drift accurately matches our limiting profile. Our results are supported by numerical simulations.

title: Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation
abstract: We prove that in rotationally invariant first-passage percolation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\geq2$, the passage time $T_n$ over a distance $n$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\exp(|T_n-μn|/n^{\frac{1}{2}(1-\varepsilon)})]\leq C$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, where $μ$ is the time constant. This implies that its variance is at most a constant times $n^{1-\varepsilon}$, the bound that Basu, Sidoravicius and Sly proved in the planar case. As in their work, our argument is an induction on the scale, but in place of their proof that the geodesic is chaotic, we use the averaging argument of Benjamini, Kalai and Schramm together with a logarithmic improvement of the Efron-Stein inequality due to Benaïm and Rossignol.

title: Delocalized region of bipartite Erdős-Rényi graphs
abstract: We consider bipartite Erdős-Rényi graphs $\mathbb{G}(n, p, d/\sqrt{np})$ with two parts of sizes $n$ and $p$, respectively, and edge probability $d/\sqrt{pn}$. We show that for $d > b_* \log (n+p)$ all eigenvectors of its adjacency matrix, with eigenvalues away from zero, are delocalized with high probability. The threshold $b_*$ is an explicit function of the size ratio $n/p$ and optimal for eigenvector delocalization near the spectral edges. Our results extend to bulk eigenvectors down to the optimal threshold $d\geq \mathcal{D}\sqrt{\log (n+p)}$ for a constant $\mathcal D \geq 1$. In the supercritical scale $d \gg \log (n+p)$ we show that all eigenvectors are delocalized. Our results also hold for sparse rectangular random matrices with independent entries.

title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

title: Permutons
abstract: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

title: The Paley--Wiener excess and a local law for the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process

title: The random matrix hard edge --- applications, exact PDFs and large $N$ expansions
abstract: A hard edge of a Hermitian random matrix occurs when the eigenvalue density is strictly zero on one side of the edge, and nonzero on the other. Another possibility is that the eigenvalues occur in $\pm$ pairs, which creates a hard edge at the origin for the positive eigenvalues. Both review material and new results are presented for random matrix ensembles exhibiting a hard edge. The review material has two focuses: one is on applications of the random matrix hard edge, while the other is on exact eigenvalue probability density functions. The new results relate to the large $N$ expansion of correlation functions and conditioned gap probability generating functions with hard edge scaling for the Jacobi ensemble. For all even $β$ we are able to show that these quantities admit expansions in inverse even powers of the variable $N_{\rm hJ}':= N - 1/2 + (a + b + 1)/β$. For the $β=2$ Jacobi unitary ensemble, we can relate the leading (next leading) correction to the limit law to a particular second order (fourth order) differential operator applied to the latter. The analogous second order differential operator is found for $β=1,4$, leading then to its conjectured form for all $β>0$.

title: Thermalization of coarse-grained variables in the Toda lattice: a numerical study
abstract: We present here a numerical study of the Toda lattice Hamiltonian dynamics showing how, despite model integrability, it is possible to find many macroscopic observables which display standard equilibrium behavior. In particular, we study numerically the energy time correlation of certain coarse-grained variables, showing that it decays with either exponential or stretched exponential behaviour, thus indicating good thermalization properties. The spirit of our observation is complementary to that of standard Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou-like numerical experiments, in which the breaking of integrability is regarded as the key ingredient for relaxation to thermal equilibrium. The present communication corroborates, on the contrary, the view that integrability is not an obstacle to thermalization, provided that a sufficiently weak definition of the latter is accepted. In the Toda lattice we have introduced several kinds of coarse-grained variables, constructed with the purpose to maintain a thermodynamic relevance also for large system sizes, which all show good thermalization properties.

title: A Geometric Construction of the Radial Dunkl and Heckman-Opdam Processes
abstract: We provide a geometric construction of the radial Dunkl and Heckman-Opdam processes for arbitrary root systems and arbitrary nonnegative real root multiplicity parameters. This is a broad class of processes including the classical Bessel process, Dyson Brownian motion, and the Dyson Bessel process. We find that, when $x_t$ is a certain anisotropic Markov diffusion process in a symmetric space $G/K$ or its tangent space at the origin, invariant under an appropriate $K$-action, the evolution in the space of orbits can be described as a radial Dunkl or Heckman-Opdam process (respective to whether the diffusion is on the tangent space or $G/K$ itself). These processes can have arbitrary nonnegative real root multiplicities, analogous to arbitrary values of $β$ in Dyson Brownian motion. In a freezing limit, analogous to $β\to \infty$ for Dyson Brownian motion, these processes become motion by mean curvature of the orbits. A connection to finite free probability is also discussed, in which we provide a geometric interpretation of certain properties related to finite free position.

title: On some stochastic evolutions on Laguerre-Polya functions
abstract: We prove uniqueness in law for three stochastic evolutions on normalised Laguerre-Pólya functions arising as scaling limits of matrix characteristic polynomial dynamics. The method of proof relies on some integrable structure of the problem in the special form of a new duality with finite-dimensional diffusions which is closely related to intertwinings.

title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.

title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
abstract: We prove that the centered height function of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble converges for each $β>0$, under rescaling of space and time variables, towards the Gaussian free field in the half-plane. The conformal structure for GFF involves the spatial change of coordinate $x\mapsto \sqrt{-x}$. The $β$--dependence is isolated in the field rescaling by $\sqrtβ$. For the proofs we study the asymptotic expansions of the moments of Laplace transforms of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble developed in our previous work with Xu.
