title: Extremes of $2d$ Coulomb gas: universal intermediate deviation regime
abstract: In this paper, we study the extreme statistics in the complex Ginibre ensemble of $N \times N$ random matrices with complex Gaussian entries, but with no other symmetries. All the $N$ eigenvalues are complex random variables and their joint distribution can be interpreted as a $2d$ Coulomb gas with a logarithmic repulsion between any pair of particles and in presence of a confining harmonic potential $v(r) \propto r^2$. We study the statistics of the eigenvalue with the largest modulus $r_{\max}$ in the complex plane. The typical and large fluctuations of $r_{\max}$ around its mean had been studied before, and they match smoothly to the right of the mean. However, it remained a puzzle to understand why the large and typical fluctuations to the left of the mean did not match. In this paper, we show that there is indeed an intermediate fluctuation regime that interpolates smoothly between the large and the typical fluctuations to the left of the mean. Moreover, we compute explicitly this "intermediate deviation function" (IDF) and show that it is universal, i.e. independent of the confining potential $v(r)$ as long as it is spherically symmetric and increases faster than $\ln r^2$ for large $r$ with an unbounded support. If the confining potential $v(r)$ has a finite support, i.e. becomes infinite beyond a finite radius, we show via explicit computation that the corresponding IDF is different. Interestingly, in the borderline case where the confining potential grows very slowly as $v(r) \sim \ln r^2$ for $r \gg 1$ with an unbounded support, the intermediate regime disappears and there is a smooth matching between the central part and the left large deviation regime.

title: Orthogonal stochastic duality functions from Lie algebra representations

title: An appetizer to modern developments on the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class
abstract: The Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) universality class describes a broad range of non-equilibrium fluctuations, including those of growing interfaces, directed polymers and particle transport, to name but a few. Mathematical physics has played a central role since then, leading to a myriad of new developments, but their implications are clearly not limited to mathematics -- as a matter of fact, it can also be studied experimentally. The aim of these lecture notes is to provide an introduction to the field that is accessible to non-specialists, reviewing basic properties of the KPZ class and highlighting main physical outcomes of mathematical developments since the year 2000. It is written in a brief and self-contained manner, with emphasis put on physical intuitions and implications, while only a small (and mostly not the latest) fraction of mathematical developments could be covered. Liquid-crystal experiments by the author and coworkers are also reviewed.

title: Asymptotics of free fermions in a quadratic well at finite temperature and the Moshe-Neuberger-Shapiro random matrix model

title: Truncated linear statistics associated with the eigenvalues of random matrices II. Partial sums over proper time delays for chaotic quantum dots
abstract: Invariant ensembles of random matrices are characterized by the distribution of their eigenvalues $\{\lambda_1,\cdots,\lambda_N\}$. title: Memory and universality in interface growth
abstract: Understanding possible universal properties for systems far from equilibrium is much less developed than for their equilibrium counterparts and poses a major challenge to present day statistical physics. This may give insight into memory effects in a broader class of far-from-equilibrium systems.

title: Phase transitions and edge scaling of number variance in Gaussian random matrices

title: Nonlinear fluctuations of weakly asymmetric interacting particle systems

title: Random matrices: Localization of the eigenvalues and the necessity of four moments
abstract: Consider the eigenvalues $\lambda_i(M_n)$ (in increasing order) of a random Hermitian matrix $M_n$ whose upper-triangular entries are independent with mean zero and variance one, and are exponentially decaying. By Wigner's semicircular law, one expects that $\lambda_i(M_n)$ concentrates around $\gamma_i \sqrt n$, where $\int_{-\infty}^{\gamma_i} \rho_{sc} (x) dx = \frac{i}{n}$ and $\rho_{sc}$ is the semicircular function. In this paper, we show that if the entries have vanishing third moment, then for all $1\le i \le n$ $$\E |\lambda_i(M_n)-\sqrt{n} \gamma_i|^2 = O(\min(n^{-c} \min(i,n+1-i)^{-2/3} n^{2/3}, n^{1/3+\eps})) ,$$ for some absolute constant $c>0$ and any absolute constant $\eps>0$. In particular, for the eigenvalues in the bulk ($\min \{i, n-i\}=\Theta (n)$), $$\E |\lambda_i(M_n)-\sqrt{n} \gamma_i|^2 = O(n^{-c}). $$ \noindent A similar result is achieved for the rate of convergence. As a corollary, we show that the four moment condition in the Four Moment Theorem is necessary, in the sense that if one allows the fourth moment to change (while keeping the first three moments fixed), then the \emph{mean} of $\lambda_i(M_n)$ changes by an amount comparable to $n^{-1/2}$ on the average. We make a precise conjecture about how the expectation of the eigenvalues vary with the fourth moment.

title: Extremal statistics of curved growing interfaces in 1+1 dimensions
abstract: We study the joint probability distribution function (pdf) of the maximum M of the height and its position X_M of a curved growing interface belonging to the universality class described by the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation in 1+1 dimensions. We obtain exact results for the closely related problem of p non-intersecting Brownian bridges where we compute the joint pdf P_p(M,\tau_M) where \tau_M is there the time at which the maximal height M is reached. Our analytical results, in the limit p \to \infty, become exact for the interface problem in the growth regime. We show that our results, for moderate values of p \sim 10 describe accurately our numerical data of a prototype of these systems, the polynuclear growth model in droplet geometry. We also discuss applications of our results to the ground state configuration of the directed polymer in a random potential with one fixed endpoint.

title: Universality for generalized Wigner matrices with Bernoulli distribution
abstract: The universality for the eigenvalue spacing statistics of generalized Wigner matrices was established in our previous work \cite{EYY} under certain conditions on the probability distributions of the matrix elements. A major class of probability measures excluded in \cite{EYY} are the Bernoulli measures. In this paper, we extend the universality result of \cite{EYY} to include the Bernoulli measures so that the only restrictions on the probability distributions of the matrix elements are the subexponential decay and the normalization condition that the variances in each row sum up to one. The new ingredient is a strong local semicircle law which improves the error estimate on the Stieltjes transform of the empirical measure of the eigenvalues from the order $(N \eta)^{-1/2}$ to $(N \eta)^{-1}$. Here $\eta$ is the imaginary part of the spectral parameter in the definition of the Stieltjes transform and $N$ is the size of the matrix.

title: Totally Asymmetric Zero-Range process in the Rarefaction Fan
abstract: We consider the one-dimensional totally asymmetric zero-range process starting from a step decreasing profile leading in the hydrodynamic limit to the rarefaction fan of the associate hydrodynamic equation. Under that initial condition, we show that the weighted sum of joint probabilities for second class particles sharing the same site, is convergent and we compute its limit. We derive the Law of Large Numbers for the position of a second class particle initially at the origin under the initial state in which all positive sites are empty and all negative sites are occupied and also for a slight perturbation of the invariant state.

title: Phase Transitions in the Distribution of Bipartite Entanglement of a Random Pure State
abstract: Using a Coulomb gas method, we compute analytically the probability distribution of the Renyi entropies (a standard measure of entanglement) for a random pure state of a large bipartite quantum system. We show that, for any order q>1 of the Renyi entropy, there are two critical values at which the entropy's probability distribution changes shape. These critical points correspond to two different transitions in the corresponding charge density of the Coulomb gas: the disappearance of an integrable singularity at the origin and the detachement of a single-charge drop from the continuum sea of all the other charges. These transitions respectively control the left and right tails of the entropy's probability distribution, as verified also by Monte Carlo numerical simulations of the Coulomb gas equilibrium dynamics.

title: Probability distributions of Linear Statistics in Chaotic Cavities and associated phase transitions
abstract: We establish large deviation formulas for linear statistics on the $N$ transmission eigenvalues $\{T_i\}$ of a chaotic cavity, in the framework of Random Matrix Theory. Given any linear statistics of interest $A=\sum_{i=1}^N a(T_i)$, the probability distribution $\mathcal{P}_A(A,N)$ of $A$ generically satisfies the large deviation formula $\lim_{N\to\infty}[-2\log\mathcal{P}_A(Nx,N)/\beta N^2]=\Psi_A(x)$, where $\Psi_A(x)$ is a rate function that we compute explicitly in many cases (conductance, shot noise, moments) and $\beta$ corresponds to different symmetry classes. Using these large deviation expressions, it is possible to recover easily known results and to produce new formulas, such as a closed form expression for $v(n)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathrm{var}(\mathcal{T}_n)$ (where $\mathcal{T}_n=\sum_{i}T_i^n$) for arbitrary integer $n$. The universal limit $v^\star=\lim_{n\to\infty} v(n)=1/2\pi\beta$ is also computed exactly. The distributions display a central Gaussian region flanked on both sides by non-Gaussian tails. At the junction of the two regimes, weakly non-analytical points appear, a direct consequence of phase transitions in an associated Coulomb gas problem. Numerical checks are also provided, which are in full agreement with our asymptotic results in both real and Laplace space even for moderately small $N$. Part of the results have been announced in [P. Vivo, S.N. Majumdar and O. Bohigas, {\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} {\bf 101}, 216809 (2008)].

title: Random matrices: Universality of local eigenvalue statistics up to the edge
abstract: This is a continuation of our earlier paper on the universality of the eigenvalues of Wigner random matrices. The main new results of this paper are an extension of the results in that paper from the bulk of the spectrum up to the edge. In particular, we prove a variant of the universality results of Soshnikov for the largest eigenvalues, assuming moment conditions rather than symmetry conditions. The main new technical observation is that there is a significant bias in the Cauchy interlacing law near the edge of the spectrum which allows one to continue ensuring the delocalization of eigenvectors.

title: Bulk universality for Wigner hermitian matrices with subexponential decay
abstract: We consider the ensemble of $n \times n$ Wigner hermitian matrices $H = (h_{\ell k})_{1 \leq \ell,k \leq n}$ that generalize the Gaussian unitary ensemble (GUE). The matrix elements $h_{k\ell} = \bar h_{\ell k}$ are given by $h_{\ell k} = n^{-1/2} (x_{\ell k} + \sqrt{-1} y_{\ell k})$, where $x_{\ell k}, y_{\ell k}$ for $1 \leq \ell < k \leq n$ are i.i.d. random variables with mean zero and variance 1/2, $y_{\ell\ell}=0$ and $x_{\ell \ell}$ have mean zero and variance 1. We assume the distribution of $x_{\ell k}, y_{\ell k}$ to have subexponential decay. In a recent paper, four of the authors recently established that the gap distribution and averaged $k$-point correlation of these matrices were \emph{universal} (and in particular, agreed with those for GUE) assuming additional regularity hypotheses on the $x_{\ell k}, y_{\ell k}$. In another recent paper, the other two authors, using a different method, established the same conclusion assuming instead some moment and support conditions on the $x_{\ell k}, y_{\ell k}$. In this short note we observe that the arguments of these two papers can be combined to establish universality of the gap distribution and averaged $k$-point correlations for all Wigner matrices (with subexponentially decaying entries), with no extra assumptions.

title: Zeros of Airy Function and Relaxation Process
abstract: One-dimensional system of Brownian motions called Dyson's model is the particle system with long-range repulsive forces acting between any pair of particles, where the strength of force is $\beta/2$ times the inverse of particle distance. When $\beta=2$, it is realized as the Brownian motions in one dimension conditioned never to collide with each other. For any initial configuration, it is proved that Dyson's model with $\beta=2$ and $N$ particles, $\X(t)=(X_1(t), ..., X_N(t)), t \in [0,\infty), 2 \leq N < \infty$, is determinantal in the sense that any multitime correlation function is given by a determinant with a continuous kernel. The Airy function $\Ai(z)$ is an entire function with zeros all located on the negative part of the real axis $\R$. We consider Dyson's model with $\beta=2$ starting from the first $N$ zeros of $\Ai(z)$, $0 > a_1 > ... > a_N$, $N \geq 2$. In order to properly control the effect of such initial confinement of particles in the negative region of $\R$, we put the drift term to each Brownian motion, which increases in time as a parabolic function : $Y_j(t) = X_j(t) + t^2/4 + \{d_1 + \sum_{\ell=1}^N (1/a_{\ell})\}t, 1 \leq j \leq N$, where $d_1=\Ai'(0)/\Ai(0)$. We show that, as the $N \to \infty$ limit of $\Y(t)=(Y_1(t), ..., Y_N(t)), t \in [0, \infty)$, we obtain an infinite particle system, which is the relaxation process from the configuration, in which every zero of $\Ai(z)$ on the negative $\R$ is occupied by one particle, to the stationary state $\mu_{\Ai}$. The stationary state $\mu_{\Ai}$ is the determinantal point process with the Airy kernel, which is spatially inhomogeneous on $\R$ and in which the Tracy-Widom distribution describes the rightmost particle position.

title: Mesoscopic colonization of a spectral band
abstract: We consider the unitary matrix model in the limit where the size of the matrices become infinite and in the critical situation when a new spectral band is about to emerge. In previous works the number of expected eigenvalues in a neighborhood of the band was fixed and finite, a situation that was termed "birth of a cut" or "first colonization". We now consider the transitional regime where this microscopic population in the new band grows without bounds but at a slower rate than the size of the matrix. The local population in the new band organizes in a "mesoscopic" regime, in between the macroscopic behavior of the full system and the previously studied microscopic one. The mesoscopic colony may form a finite number of new bands, with a maximum number dictated by the degree of criticality of the original potential. We describe the delicate scaling limit that realizes/controls the mesoscopic colony. The method we use is the steepest descent analysis of the Riemann-Hilbert problem that is satisfied by the associated orthogonal polynomials.

title: Non-intersecting Brownian Interfaces and Wishart Random Matrices
authors:
Satya N. Majumdar (Laboratoire de Physique
  Th'eorique et Mod`eles Statistiques
abstract: We study a system of $N$ non-intersecting $(1+1)$-dimensional fluctuating elastic interfaces (`vicious bridges') at thermal equilibrium, each subject to periodic boundary condition in the longitudinal direction and in presence of a substrate that induces an external confining potential for each interface. We show that, for a large system and with an appropriate choice of the external confining potential, the joint distribution of the heights of the $N$ non-intersecting interfaces at a fixed point on the substrate can be mapped to the joint distribution of the eigenvalues of a Wishart matrix of size $N$ with complex entries (Dyson index $\beta=2$), thus providing a physical realization of the Wishart matrix. Exploiting this analogy to random matrix, we calculate analytically (i) the average density of states of the interfaces (ii) the height distribution of the uppermost and lowermost interfaces (extrema) and (iii) the asymptotic (large $N$) distribution of the center of mass of the interfaces. In the last case, we show that the probability density of the center of mass has an essential singularity around its peak which is shown to be a direct consequence of a phase transition in an associated Coulomb gas problem.

title: Random matrices: The distribution of the smallest singular values
abstract: Let $\a$ be a real-valued random variable of mean zero and variance 1. Let $M_n(\a)$ denote the $n \times n$ random matrix whose entries are iid copies of $\a$ and $\sigma_n(M_n(\a))$ denote the least singular value of $M_n(\a)$. ($\sigma_n(M_n(\a))^2$ is also usually interpreted as the least eigenvalue of the Wishart matrix $M_n M_n^{\ast}$.) We show that (under a finite moment assumption) the probability distribution $n \sigma_n(M_n(\a))^2$ is {\it universal} in the sense that it does not depend on the distribution of $\a$. In particular, it converges to the same limiting distribution as in the special case when $a$ is real gaussian. (The limiting distribution was computed explicitly in this case by Edelman.) We also proved a similar result for complex-valued random variables of mean zero, with real and imaginary parts having variance 1/2 and covariance zero. Similar results are also obtained for the joint distribution of the bottom $k$ singular values of $M_n(\a)$ for any fixed $k$ (or even for $k$ growing as a small power of $n$) and for rectangular matrices. Our approach is motivated by the general idea of "property testing" from combinatorics and theoretical computer science. This seems to be a new approach in the study of spectra of random matrices and combines tools from various areas of mathematics.

title: Non-Equilibrium Dynamics of Dyson's Model with an Infinite Number of Particles
abstract: Dyson's model is a one-dimensional system of Brownian motions with long-range repulsive forces acting between any pair of particles with strength proportional to the inverse of distances with proportionality constant $\beta/2$. For example, we obtain the relaxation process starting from a configuration, in which every point of $\Z$ is occupied by one particle, to the stationary state, which is the determinantal point process with the sine kernel.

title: Distributions of Conductance and Shot Noise and Associated Phase Transitions
abstract: For a chaotic cavity with two indentical leads each supporting N channels, we compute analytically, for large N, the full distribution of the conductance and the shot noise power and show that in both cases there is a central Gaussian region flanked on both sides by non-Gaussian tails. title: Maximum distributions of bridges of noncolliding Brownian paths
abstract: The one-dimensional Brownian motion starting from the origin at time $t=0$, conditioned to return to the origin at time $t=1$ and to stay positive during time interval $0 < t < 1$, is called the Bessel bridge with duration 1. We consider the $N$-particle system of such Bessel bridges conditioned never to collide with each other in $0 < t < 1$, which is the continuum limit of the vicious walk model in watermelon configuration with a wall. Distributions of maximum-values of paths attained in the time interval $t \in (0,1)$ are studied to characterize the statistics of random patterns of the repulsive paths on the spatio-temporal plane. For the outermost path, the distribution function of maximum value is exactly determined for general $N$. We show that the present $N$-path system of noncolliding Bessel bridges is realized as the positive-eigenvalue process of the $2N \times 2N$ matrix-valued Brownian bridge in the symmetry class C. Using this fact computer simulations are performed and numerical results on the $N$-dependence of the maximum-value distributions of the inner paths are reported. The present work demonstrates that the extreme-value problems of noncolliding paths are related with the random matrix theory, representation theory of symmetry, and the number theory.

title: Exact distribution of the maximal height of p vicious walkers
abstract: Using path integral techniques, we compute exactly the distribution of the maximal height H_p of p nonintersecting Brownian walkers over a unit time interval in one dimension, both for excursions (p-watermelons with a wall) and bridges (p-watermelons without a wall), for all integer p\ge 1. For large p, we show that < H_p > \sim \sqrt{2p} (excursions) whereas < H_p > \sim \sqrt{p} (bridges). Our exact results prove that previous numerical experiments only measured the pre-asymptotic behaviors and not the correct asymptotic ones. In addition, our method establishes a physical connection between vicious walkers and random matrix theory.

title: The Cauchy two-matrix model
abstract: We introduce a new class of two(multi)-matrix models of positive Hermitean matrices coupled in a chain; the coupling is related to the Cauchy kernel and differs from the exponential coupling more commonly used in similar models. The correlation functions are expressed entirely in terms of certain biorthogonal polynomials and solutions of appropriate Riemann-Hilbert problems, thus paving the way to a steepest descent analysis and universality results. The interpretation of the formal expansion of the partition function in terms of multicolored ribbon-graphs is provided and a connection to the O(1) model. A steepest descent analysis of the partition function reveals that the model is related to a trigonal curve (three-sheeted covering of the plane) much in the same way as the Hermitean matrix model is related to a hyperelliptic curve.

title: First Colonization of a Spectral Outpost in Random Matrix Theory
abstract: We describe the distribution of the first finite number of eigenvalues in a newly-forming band of the spectrum of the random Hermitean matrix model. The method is rigorously based on the Riemann-Hilbert analysis of the corresponding orthogonal polynomials. We provide an analysis with an error term of order N^(-2 h) where 1/h = 2 nu+2 is the exponent of non-regularity of the effective potential, thus improving even in the usual case the analysis of the pertinent literature. The behavior of the first finite number of zeroes (eigenvalues) appearing in the new band is analyzed and connected with the location of the zeroes of certain Freud polynomials. In general all these newborn zeroes approach the point of nonregularity at the rate N^(-h) whereas one (a stray zero) lags behind at a slower rate of approach. The kernels for the correlator functions in the scaling coordinate near the emerging band are provided together with the subleading term: in particular the transition between K and K+1 eigenvalues is analyzed in detail.

title: Exact Minimum Eigenvalue Distribution of an Entangled Random Pure State
abstract: A recent conjecture regarding the average of the minimum eigenvalue of the reduced density matrix of a random complex state is proved. title: Vacancy localization in the square dimer model
abstract: We study the classical dimer model on a square lattice with a single vacancy by developing a graph-theoretic classification of the set of all configurations which extends the spanning tree formulation of close-packed dimers. With this formalism, we can address the question of the possible motion of the vacancy induced by dimer slidings. We find a probability 57/4-10Sqrt[2] for the vacancy to be strictly jammed in an infinite system. More generally, the size distribution of the domain accessible to the vacancy is characterized by a power law decay with exponent 9/8. On a finite system, the probability that a vacancy in the bulk can reach the boundary falls off as a power law of the system size with exponent 1/4. The resultant weak localization of vacancies still allows for unbounded diffusion, characterized by a diffusion exponent that we relate to that of diffusion on spanning trees. We also implement numerical simulations of the model with both free and periodic boundary conditions.

title: Tagged Particle Correlations in the Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process: Finite Size Effects
abstract: We study finite size effects in the variance of the displacement of a tagged particle in the stationary state of the Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process (ASEP) on a ring of size $L$. The process involves hard core particles undergoing stochastic driven dynamics on a lattice. The variance of the displacement of the tagged particle, averaged with respect to an initial stationary ensemble and stochastic evolution, grows linearly with time at both small and very large times. We find that at intermediate times, it shows oscillations with a well defined size-dependent period. These oscillations arise from sliding density fluctuations (SDF) in the stationary state with respect to the drift of the tagged particle, the density fluctuations being transported through the system by kinematic waves. In the general context of driven diffusive systems, both the Edwards-Wilkinson (EW) and the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) fixed points are unstable with respect to the SDF fixed point, a flow towards which is generated on adding a gradient term to the EW and the KPZ time-evolution equation. We also study tagged particle correlations for a fixed initial configuration, drawn from the stationary ensemble, following earlier work by van Beijeren. We find that the time dependence of this correlation is determined by the dissipation of the density fluctuations. We show that an exactly solvable linearized model captures the essential qualitative features seen in the finite size effects of the tagged particle correlations in the ASEP. Moreover, this linearized model also provides an exact coarse-grained description of two other microscopic models.

title: Random Matrices, the Ulam Problem, Directed Polymers & Growth Models, and Sequence Matching
abstract: In these lecture notes I will give a pedagogical introduction to some common aspects of 4 different problems: (i) random matrices (ii) the longest increasing subsequence problem (also known as the Ulam problem) (iii) directed polymers in random medium and growth models in (1+1) dimensions and (iv) a problem on the alignment of a pair of random sequences. Each of these problems is almost entirely a sub-field by itself and here I will discuss only some specific aspects of each of them. These 4 problems have been studied almost independently for the past few decades, but only over the last few years a common thread was found to link all of them. In particular all of them share one common limiting probability distribution known as the Tracy-Widom distribution that describes the asymptotic probability distribution of the largest eigenvalue of a random matrix. I will mention here, without mathematical derivation, some of the beautiful results discovered in the past few years. Then, I will consider two specific models (a) a ballistic deposition growth model and (b) a model of sequence alignment known as the Bernoulli matching model and discuss, in some detail, how one derives exactly the Tracy-Widom law in these models. The emphasis of these lectures would be on how to map one model to another. Some open problems are discussed at the end.

title: Nonintersecting Paths, Noncolliding Diffusion Processes and Representation Theory
abstract: The system of one-dimensional symmetric simple random walks, in which none of walkers have met others in a given time period, is called the vicious walker model. Each vicious walk of $N$ walkers is represented by an $N$-tuple of nonintersecting lattice paths on the spatio-temporal plane. There is established a simple bijection between nonintersecting lattice paths and semistandard Young tableaux. Based on this bijection and some knowledge of symmetric polynomials called the Schur functions, we can give a determinantal expression to the partition function of vicious walks, which is regarded as a special case of the Karlin-McGregor formula in the probability theory (or the Lindstr\"om-Gessel-Viennot formula in the enumerative combinatorics). Due to a basic property of Schur function, we can take the diffusion scaling limit of the vicious walks and define a noncolliding system of Brownian particles. This diffusion process solves the stochastic differential equations with the drift terms acting as the repulsive two-body forces proportional to the inverse of distances between particles, and thus it is identified with Dyson's Brownian motion model. In other words, the obtained noncolliding system of Brownian particles is equivalent in distribution with the eigenvalue process of a Hermitian matrix-valued process.

The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $τ\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $τ\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.

title: Duality and hidden symmetries for time-inhomogeneous Markov processes
abstract: We study the notion of duality in the setting of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. We define duality with time-dependent duality functions. We establish the connection between duality and time-dependent symmetries and intertwinings. We illustrate the abstract results with examples from interacting particle systems and diffusion processes.

title: A simple proof of the Bourgade-Sodin-Zeitouni theorem on the excess of the sine-$β$ process for non-integer $\sqrt{2/β}>1$
abstract: We give an alternative proof of the Bourgade-Sodin-Zeitouni theorem on the excess of the sine-$β$ process for the Paley-Wiener space when $\sqrt{2/β}\in (1,+\infty)$ is not an integer. The same conclusion holds for each Bernstein space $\mathcal{B}^p$ of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$-integrable functions with $m(β)<p<\infty$, where $m(β)=β(k(β)+1)-\sqrt{β^2(k(β)+1)^2-2β}$.

title: Chasing the KPZ exponents
abstract: Forty years after it was written down, the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation is the paradigm of scale invariance far from equilibrium. In one dimension it has been solved exactly and confirmed by precision experiments, and its scaling has now been observed in two-dimensional polariton condensates. Above one dimension, however, not a single exponent is known exactly, and even the existence of an upper critical dimension is disputed. In this Perspective we argue that firm statements need not wait for exact solutions. Treating the nonlinearity as an effective noise that acts on a fractal subset of the substrate leads to bounds on the roughness exponent, $1/(d+1)\leα\le 1/d$ in $d$ dimensions. We examine the assumptions behind these bounds, confront them with four decades of theory, simulations and the new experiments, and identify the tests---foremost in three and more dimensions---that would establish or refute them.

title: Painlevé transcendents in the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions
abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions \begin{align*} &iq_t+ q_{xx}-2\left(|q|^2-1\right)q +i\left(q_{xxx}-6|q|^2q_x\right)=0,\\ &q(x,0)=q_0(x)\to\pm 1, \quad x\to\pm\infty, \end{align*} which can be characterized using a Riemann-Hilbert problem through the inverse scattering transform. With the $\bar{\partial}$-steepest descent method and double scaling limit technique, we derive the long-time asymptotics of the solution in two transition regions \begin{align*} \mathcal{P}_{a} :=\left\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}: \left| {x}/{t}-a\right|t^{2/3}<C\right\}, \quad a\in\{-4,-8\}, \end{align*} where $C>0$ is a constant. It is shown that the asymptotic expansions in two transition regions can be expressed in terms of the Hastings--McLeod solution of the Painlevé II equation in the generic case and Ablowitz--Segur solutions in the non-generic case.

title: Low-dimensional optimal stopping with rank-dependent loss
abstract: Sequential selection problems with independent observable scores and rank-dependent objectives are not reducible, in general, to dynamic optimisation over a state space of fixed dimension. We consider optimal stopping problems with truncated loss structures through the lens of the planar Poisson process, where self-similarity removes the time variable and the state is reduced to the $m$ lowest scores observed so far, rescaled to the initial time. For $m=1$ the optimal rule stops at the first record below a hyperbola, which is found by a sliding-window argument. For $m=2$ we derive the equations for the boundaries of the stopping sets of $1$-records and $2$-records, solve them explicitly on a part of the state space, and express the optimal values by quadratures. The value function and the optimal strategy are characterised by a static integro-differential equation. The optimal strategies are compared with simple low-parameter rules, which are close to optimality.

title: Complex Moments of the Derivative of the Riemann Zeta Function
abstract: We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model. For each fixed $σ>1/2$ and every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$, we show, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, that the $2s$-th moment of $|ζ'(σ+\mathrm{i}t)|$ over $t\in[1,T]$ converges, as $T\to\infty$, to the corresponding moment of the derivative of the random Euler product. We then establish, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula for the latter moment as $σ\downarrow 1/2$ throughout the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. For positive real moments, our approach is based on a change-of-measure argument and a Gaussian limit theorem for the logarithmic derivative under a tilted probability measure. For general complex moments, we combine Fourier analysis of weighted complex measures with regularized Riesz distributions. As an application, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, we resolve the conjecture of Simm and Wei [J. Lond. Math. Soc. 113 (2026)] on the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function for every $s\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. We establish the predicted asymptotic formula as $σ\downarrow1/2$, with the leading order $s^2+2s$ and an explicit leading coefficient involving an arithmetic factor and the confluent hypergeometric function of the first kind. The conjecture also holds unconditionally when $\operatorname{Re}(s)\in (0,2)$.

title: Universality of Brown measure convergence for non-Gaussian matrix polynomials with adjoints
abstract: Let $P$ be a noncommutative polynomial of arbitrary degree. We prove that the empirical spectral distribution of $P$ evaluated at independent Wigner matrices converges weakly in probability to its Brown measure limit. The same conclusion holds for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent iid matrices and their adjoints. The entry laws have bounded real or joint planar densities and a finite $(2+\varepsilon)$ moment; only second moments are required on the Wigner diagonal. The real and imaginary parts of an entry may be dependent, and its pseudovariance need not vanish. The proof develops the coefficient-algebra approach of the author's earlier work on matrix polynomials with Gaussian and non-Gaussian iid inputs \cite{Han}. The main step is a polynomial lower-tail estimate, under only second moments, for the least singular value of a tensor pencil with arbitrary fixed matrix coefficients. We use a logarithmic determinant method: a real-block small-ball argument shows that logarithmic derivatives of the determinant control the inverse pencil. Relative polynomial anti-concentration then gives the lower-tail bound. We establish convergence of logarithmic potentials by Hermitian resolvent comparison and rank truncation. This extends the recent Brown measure convergence theorem of Collins, Kitagawa, Miyagawa, Yuan and Zhong \cite{Collins} for GUE polynomials to non-Gaussian Wigner inputs.

title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation

Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

title: On stretched Kostka polynomials
abstract: Stretched Kostka polynomials are defined by $f_{λ,μ}(N) := K_{Nλ,Nμ}$, where $K_{λ,μ}$ denotes the corresponding Kostka number. In 2004, King-Tollu-Toumazet conjectured that, for every integer $k$, there are only finitely many polynomials $f_{λ,μ}(N)$ such that $f_{λ,μ}(1)=k$. For $k=3$, KTT also conjectured that there are exactly two such polynomials. We prove both conjectures via Ehrhart theory, by counting lattice points in families of rational polytopes with a fixed set of normals.

title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
abstract: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

title: Squared Bessel particle systems with weak repulsion
abstract: We study squared Bessel particle systems with repulsion parameter $κ>0$ and dimension parameter $δ\in\mathbb R$. We prove that the singular equation has a unique global strong solution for every initial state in the closed Weyl chamber, including states with coinciding particles. The solutions have locally integrable interaction terms and spend zero Lebesgue time at pairwise collisions. We also consider the equation in which the interaction terms are set to zero at collisions. At certain integer values of $δ$, this equation admits infinitely many solution laws from suitable initial configurations. In these solutions, a block of particles can remain at zero for any prescribed time before being released. For positive initial states, we determine when zero is reached and when particles enter the negative half-line. From distinct initial positions, collisions occur almost surely for $0<κ<1$ and do not occur for $κ\ge1$. Collisions of three or more particles are excluded away from zero. We give an example of a triple collision at zero. We obtain two-sided bounds for the tails of the first-zero and first-collision times. The bounds give matching powers for the first-zero time when it is finite, and for the first-collision time in nonnegative systems when $0<κ<1$.

title: Painlevé XXXIV asymptotics for the defocusing Hirota equation with step-like initial data in transition regions
abstract: We study the long-time asymptotics of the solution of the Cauchy problem for the defocusing Hirota equation with real step-like initial data. Because of the term $α(q_{xx}-2|q|^2q)$, the backgrounds rotate in time, and the symmetry $k\mapsto-k$ of the associated Riemann--Hilbert problem is lost. As a consequence, the branch points $\pm c_l$ and $\pm c_r$ become soft edges along different critical lines. We consider the two transition regions in which the edge $-c_r$, respectively $c_l$, becomes soft, namely the $t^{-2/3}$-neighbourhoods of the lines $x/t=-6βc_r^2+2αc_r$ and $x/t=-6βc_l^2-2αc_l$. By the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method, we show that in both regions the leading correction to the rotating background is of order $t^{-1/3}$ and is a phase correction, in contrast with the order $t^{-2/3}$ known for the defocusing mKdV equation. In the first region, the correction is given by an integral of a solution of the Painlevé XXXIV equation. In the second region, the relevant Painlevé XXXIV model problem reduces to Airy functions, and the correction is a phase shift which is quadratic in $x/t$ and independent of the initial data; in addition, a stationary point of the phase function produces a contribution of order $t^{-1/2}$, which is expressed through parabolic cylinder functions.

title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
abstract: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.

title: Extreme value statistics for majorisation partial orders

title: Real zeros of Durfee polynomials: Proof of the Canfield--Corteel--Savage conjecture
abstract: We prove the conjecture of Canfield, Corteel, and Savage that for every positive integer $n$, the Durfee polynomial $D_n(x)=\sum_{d=1}^{\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor}p(n,d)x^d$ counting partitions of $n$ by the side length of their Durfee square has only real zeros. More precisely, $D_n$ has a simple zero at the origin and exactly $\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor-1$ simple negative zeros. Consequently, for every $n\ge1$, the sequence $p(n,1),\ldots,p(n,\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor)$ is strictly log-concave and unimodal. As a further consequence, the Durfee square side length of a uniformly chosen partition of $n$ has the same distribution as $1$ plus a sum of independent Bernoulli random variables.

title: Cover times of random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees

title: Fluctuations of sample eigenvalues in a spiked covariance model with Haar-rotated spikes: a transition at $p^2 \asymp n$
abstract: We study the outlying eigenvalues of a sample covariance matrix whose population covariance is itself random. The population covariance is $Σ_p=A_p+O_pB_pO_p^*+σ^2I_p$, where $A_p$ and $B_p$ are deterministic positive semidefinite matrices of fixed ranks $r$ and $s$, and where $O_p$ is Haar distributed on the orthogonal group in the real case, and on the unitary group in the complex case. Conditionally on $O_p$, we observe $n$ independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance $Σ_p$, and we build the sample covariance matrix $\widehatΣ_p$ from these vectors. The fluctuations of the spike eigenvalues of $\widehatΣ_p$ come from two different sources: the Haar matrix $O_p$, which displaces the population spikes at the scale $1/p$, and the sampling, which acts at the scale $n^{-1/2}$. Comparing these two scales amounts to comparing $p^2$ with $n$, so the ratio which governs the fluctuations is $p^2/n$, while in the classical spiked model it is the aspect ratio $p/n$. We give the limiting law of each spike in four regimes where $n,p\to \infty$. When $p/n\to c>0$, and when $p/n\to0$ with $p^2/n\to\infty$, the sampling term dominates, the limit does not depend on $O_p$ and is Gaussian, as in the classical spiked model. When $p^2/n\to0$, the Haar randomness dominates, and the limit is a weighted sum of independent $χ^2_1$ variables in the real case, and of independent exponential variables in the complex case. When $p^2/n\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, the two terms are of the same order, and the limit is the convolution of Gaussian and $χ^2_1$ or Exponential variables. We then apply these results to a linear mixed model with a continuous batch effect, in which the Haar assumption is what makes the separation of the signal and of the batch possible, and we build a test for the value of a single spike.

title: Spectrum of non-Hermitian self-normalized random matrices with heavy tails

Under a bounded density assumption, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges in probability to a deterministic law $μ_α^{\mathrm{SN}}$ on $\mathbb{C}$. This law is rotationally invariant, is supported in the closed unit disk with outer radius one, and has neither point atoms nor mass on the unit circle. The laws interpolate between $δ_0$ as $α\downarrow0$ and the circular law as $α\uparrow2$. These also describe the limiting eigenvalue distributions of $Y_n$ for real entries with slowly varying tails and for centered entries with bounded density in the normal domain of attraction, respectively. For real symmetric entries with bounded density, the spectral radius converges to one in probability for $0<α\le2$, using the upper bound of Francois, Heiny and Hu (arXiv:2608.28169). We also give a general criterion identifying the outer support radius of rotationally invariant laws from fractional moments of fresh cavity weights, under explicit trace and radial-recovery assumptions.

title: Twisted algebras of invariant formal power series over monoids
abstract: We develop a general monoid-theoretic framework to construct and study graded and color Hopf algebras of formal power series of bounded degree invariant under group actions. Rather than working with external alphabets of commuting, noncommuting, or anti-commuting variables, we start from an abstract monoid $M$ equipped with a $2$-cocycle twisting $τ:M\times M\to \mathbb{K}$, which is allowed to vanish, a bigrading over a commutative monoid $\mathcal{G}\times\mathbb{N}$ endowed with a bicharacter $ϕ$, and a group $G$ acting on $M$ via a bigraded action $ρ$ that is quasi-multiplicative with respect to $τ$, coupled with a $1$-cocycle weight function $ω:G\times M\to\mathbb{K}^\times$. By formulating local finiteness, gradings, quasi-multiplicativity, and ideals relative to the non-vanishing of $τ$, we prove that the invariant space $\mathbb{K}\langle\kern-0.2em\langle M\rangle\kern-0.2em\rangle^G$ forms a well-defined bigraded subalgebra of bounded-degree formal power series with a canonical monomial basis indexed by $ω$-admissible orbits. Furthermore, we establish four functorial constructions: embeddings into larger invariant algebras via restricted actions, color tensor product decompositions for direct products and diagonal actions, connected color Hopf algebra structures induced by internal monoid duplication, and quotient color Hopf algebras governed by invariant-retraction pairs with an explicit description of their kernel bi-ideals. As applications, we uniformly recover and extend the classical and twisted Hopf algebras of symmetric and quasisymmetric functions in commuting and noncommuting variables, MacMahon symmetric functions, the full square of symmetric and quasisymmetric Hopf algebras in superspace, symmetric and quasisymmetric functions in partially commutative variables, and signed-symmetric functions associated with the hyperoctahedral group.

title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections

The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. title: Conditional propagation of chaos for systems of particles with polynomial interactions
abstract: We consider N interacting particles taking values in the real numbers and evolving in discrete time with time step 1/n. We show that, as N and n tend to infinity, the system converges to the solution of a conditional McKean-Vlasov equation which is driven by an additional Brownian motion which emerges in the limit from the collective perturbations. Moreover we give explicit bounds for the Wasserstein-2-distance. Our proof combines the invariance principle of Mossel, O'Donnell and Oleszkiewicz (2010), the CLT for Wiener chaoses in the Wasserstein-2-form of Ledoux, Nourdin and Peccati (2015) and a conditional law of large numbers for weighted U-statistics proven in this paper.

title: Pathwise uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with a $3/4$-Hölder diffusion coefficient

On each short interval, we compare the difference of two solutions with an auxiliary linear process. An expected weighted $L^1$ bound independent of the noise multiplier, together with a vanishing sum of approximation errors, yields pathwise uniqueness. The method may also apply to other SPDEs admitting analogous linear comparison and stochastic convolution estimates.

title: Central limit theorem for linear eigenvalue statistics of random spatial networks

This generalizes the hard distance threshold of random geometric graphs and accommodates long-range connections. We also consider a weighted extension in which each vertex carries a positive random weight that influences its probability of connecting to other vertices. This combination of spatial structure and heterogeneous connectivity raises the question of whether spectral fluctuations exhibit Gaussian behavior on large scales. We address this question by studying linear eigenvalue statistics $\operatorname{Tr}[f(A_n)]$ of the adjacency matrix $A_n$ of the random connection model in expanding windows $W_n$. For polynomial test functions, we establish a finite limit for the normalized variance and prove a central limit theorem under suitable connection-profile integrability and vertex mark moment assumptions. When the limiting variance is positive, the normalized statistics admit an $O(|W_n|^{-1/2})$ normal-approximation bound in both Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distance. Furthermore, under an exponential moment assumption on the vertex marks, we extend the central limit theorem to a general class of test functions $f$.

For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

title: Stochastic Homogenization of Schrödinger Equations with Exponentially Mixing Sub-Gaussian Potentials

Dyn. 14 (2014), 1350013] to almost sure convergence. The results are non perturbative in the amplitude of $V$ and require neither Gaussian marginals nor weak randomness. We further establish a Gaussian fluctuation central limit theorem with explicit covariance. The limiting fluctuation is the solution to the linear stochastic Schrödinger equation with additive spatial white noise \begin{equation*} i\partial_t\mathcal{G} = H_0 \mathcal{G} + \sqrt{\widehat{R}(0)}\,\bar{u}\,ξ, \qquad H_0 = -Δ+ \mathbb{E}[V], \end{equation*} where $ξ$ is a time frozen spatial white noise on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathcal{G}$ takes values in $H^{-\mathfrak{s}}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for every $\mathfrak{s}>\frac{d}{2}$. The proofs combine Duhamel iteration with multiscale cluster expansion for the cumulants of smoothed linear functionals of the potential.

title: Localization transition in a spin chain with an exact Fock-space tree
abstract: Many-body localization is often pictured as Anderson localization on the graph of many-body configurations. Strongly correlated disorder and a dense net of loops, however, make this graph hard to analyze. We introduce a local disordered spin-1 chain in which a single domain wall explores an exact binary tree of configurations. Random fields create strongly correlated disorder on this tree, as in generic interacting systems, while the absence of loops keeps the problem tractable. We rigorously bound the spreading of the domain wall at strong disorder, and efficient numerics on exponentially large trees indicate a localization transition at finite disorder strength.

title: Discriminants and resultants of orthogonal polynomials
abstract: The concept of a linked pair of two sequences of polynomials, one of which is orthogonal, is introduced. Such a pair always has a resultant that factors. Two methods for producing such linked pairs are given: one for general orthogonal polynomials and the other for any polynomial in the Askey scheme. Generalized discriminants are introduced and evaluated, including a general product formula for each operator in the Askey scheme. A new notion of companion orthogonal polynomials is also introduced and used to evaluate the discriminants of orthogonal polynomials. These methods recover all known formulas for the generalized discriminants of classical polynomials and provide new ones.

title: Interacting Brownian Particles with Local Time Driven Jumps and Memory
abstract: We study a system of Brownian particles on the real line whose jump intensities are excited by pairwise collision local times and decay exponentially between encounters. For every finite number of particles and every interaction strength, we construct a global solution and prove uniqueness in law. Under mean-field scaling, exchangeable chaotic initial data, and uniform integrability of the initial intensities, we prove propagation of chaos on path space. The limit is a nonlinear jump-diffusion whose intensity is driven by the density of its own position; it is unique among such processes with locally bounded mean intensity. The proof combines uniform intensity and local-time estimates, tightness of particle and pair empirical measures, identification of conditional collision local times, and a coupling argument for nonlinear uniqueness. No moment assumptions are imposed on the initial positions or the jump-size distribution.

title: Folding of cluster algebras
abstract: We develop a general framework for folding cluster algebras from simply-laced Cartan data equipped with admissible finite-group actions. For arbitrary finite sequences, we establish folding of root data, compatible pairs, $\bfi$-box seeds, and their individual cluster variables, without reducedness, finite-type, or acyclicity assumptions. In the reduced case, the folding is realized through quantum unipotent coordinate algebras and is compatible with dual PBW generators. It sends cluster monomials associated with canonical lifted $\bfi$-box seeds to elements of the classical dual canonical basis for the quotient Cartan datum. For arbitrary positive braids in finite Cartan type, the folding is realized through quantum virtual Grothendieck rings and, after specialization at $q=1$, is induced by a single ambient Grothendieck-ring homomorphism. Finally, for arbitrary symmetrizable Cartan data and arbitrary positive braids, we prove that the Laurent homomorphism identifying corresponding seed variables restricts to a surjective algebra homomorphism between the corresponding cluster algebras. We also extend the Kimura--Oya quantum twist automorphisms to arbitrary positive braids after localization at the frozen variables, and prove that their commutative specializations commute with the folding homomorphisms.

title: Continuous-Time Random Walks with Internal Stochastic Renewal Process
abstract: We introduce a continuous-time random walk process via a structured density by tracking the state of the particle as the system evolves. Whenever the particle makes a jump, its internal state either increases by one or resets to zero, so that the internal state evolves according to a renewal process. A wide range of governing integro-differential equations may be obtained from this formulation, some of which exhibit various types of anomalous behaviour. For certain choices of reset probabilities, waiting times and jump distributions, we explicitly derive the mode-dependent memory kernels and investigate their continuum limits. The framework can recover the time-and-space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation, which traditionally models the interplay between long wait times and large jumps and exhibits anomalous diffusion. Furthermore, we obtain a process which converges toward the equilibrium distribution as time approaches some finite value through a sequence of waiting times which decrease geometrically. Finally, we investigate a process that incorporates self-excitation and self-inhibition into the waiting times for each state to produce a mean square displacement proportional to $t^ν$ for any $ν> 0$. Through these examples, we illustrate the link between the microscopic mechanisms in these processes and their non-local macroscopic governing equations.

title: Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise
abstract: In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.

title: Particle systems and the supercooled Stefan problem: Long time behaviour and fluctuations
abstract: We consider an infinite system of particles on the positive real line, initiated from a Poisson point process, which move according to Brownian motion up until the hitting time of a barrier. The barrier increases when it is hit, allowing for the possibility of sequences of successive jumps to occur instantaneously. The scaling limit gives a representation for the supercooled Stefan problem and its free boundary, from which we can determine the asymptotic limit for the barrier movement. We establish also a functional central limit theorem describing the fluctuations about this limit, from which we can determine the rate of convergence for particle system approximations to the supercooled Stefan problem under ``weak feedback" assumptions introduced in arXiv:1811.12356. We finally show that these fluctuations are identical to the fluctuations of a continuous analogue to 1D-MDLA.

title: Higher order convergence rate in probability for approximations of the stochastic Burgers and Cahn-Hilliard equation
abstract: We consider temporal approximations of stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise, with nonlinearities that may lose both integrability and regularity. Our key examples are the stochastic Burgers equation in dimension 1 and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in dimensions $\leq 3$. We show that the accelerated exponential Euler scheme achieves a rate of convergence in probability that is well beyond the state of the art: arbitrarily close to $3/4$ in the case of Burgers and $1-d/8$ in the case of Cahn-Hilliard.

title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
abstract: We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare their hitting probabilities with those of the time-homogeneous walk obtained by fixing the conductances at the starting time. These estimates give proofs of two results established in greater generality by Li and Park: if the upper network is recurrent, every vertex is visited infinitely often almost surely; if the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite. In a finite domain, the difference between the two exit probabilities is bounded by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. We obtain a corresponding infinite-volume estimate for the probability of never hitting a given vertex. To prove these estimates, we compare two Dirichlet forms and use a contraction property of the killed transition operators. We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$.

title: Hopf algebras of leaf-graded forests
abstract: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.
